summary: This research introduces LLM4EHR, a method that uses large language models to align clinical time series with medical event sequences for outcome predictions in intensive care units. It leverages foundation models pre-trained on complex clinical data.

title: Relevant and Irrelevant: A Renormalization Group Analysis of Transformer Attention
summary: This paper uses Wilsonian renormalization group theory to analyze the Transformer's attention mechanism, treating it as a perturbation of the MLP residual-stack fixed point. It investigates whether attention acts as a relevant, marginal, or irrelevant operator.

title: Looped Latent Attention: Cross-Loop KV Compression for Looped Transformers
summary: This research introduces Looped Latent Attention for Looped Transformers, which compresses K/V caches across recurrence steps. It aims to reduce decoding memory requirements by exploiting the structured nature of loop-indexed caches.

title: Robust Peak-cost Constrained Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper studies Robust Peak-cost Constrained Reinforcement Learning (RP-CRL), an approach to maximize expected reward while controlling the maximum cost along a trajectory. It is motivated by safety-critical applications where large violations are catastrophic.

title: ADS-C: Antidistillation Sampling for Classification
summary: This research proposes Antidistillation Sampling for Classification (ADS-C), a method to counter knowledge distillation attacks against proprietary classifiers. It uses input-dependent gradient-based sampling to protect model integrity.

title: Deep Learning Approaches for Sleep Apnea Classification from Polysomnographic EEG Signals
summary: This paper explores deep learning approaches for classifying sleep apnea from polysomnographic EEG signals, aiming to automate and improve the resource-intensive diagnosis process. It detects central nervous system effects of sleep apnea events.

title: Inpainting Insights: Elevating Visual XAI with Photorealistic Perturbations
summary: This research enhances visual Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) through photorealistic perturbation-based methods to better interpret complex machine learning models. It aims to make AI model behavior more understandable.

title: Diffusion models recover accurate mixture weights despite score function insensitivity
summary: This paper investigates how score-based generative diffusion models recover accurate mixture weights even with score function insensitivity, resolving a paradox in their behavior regarding multimodal distribution learning.

title: Rethinking Transfer in Continual Learning: A Replay-Based Realisation
summary: This research rethinks transfer in continual learning for language models, proposing a replay-based realization to enable models to acquire new tasks efficiently without expensive retraining. It aims to improve continuous adaptation.

title: Do Generative Models Keep Time? A Time-Aware Evaluation of Synthetic Sequential Tabular Data
summary: This research introduces a time-aware evaluation method for synthetic sequential tabular data generated by generative models. It assesses whether these models accurately maintain temporal consistency, such as timestamps and entity paths.

title: ASK-NN: An Asymmetric Nearest-Neighbor Test that detects Distribution Drifts in Natural Language
summary: This research introduces ASK-NN, an asymmetric nearest-neighbor test designed to detect distribution drifts in natural language, particularly useful for identifying hallucinations and artificial text in LLM-generated outputs.

title: Toward Federated Multimodal Graph Foundation Models: A Topology-Aware Multimodal Alignment Framework
summary: This research proposes a topology-aware multimodal alignment framework for Federated Multimodal Graph Foundation Models. It aims to enable robust learning on multimodal-attributed graphs in distributed environments.

title: A Benchmark for Electrical Load Forecasting Across Grid Levels: Time-Series Transformers Outperform Established Methods
summary: This paper introduces a comprehensive benchmark for electrical load forecasting across various grid levels, demonstrating that Time-Series Transformers outperform established methods. It provides evaluation of AI models in smart grid applications.

title: CardioMeta: Calibrated Multi-Task Prediction of Diabetes, Hypertension, and Cardiovascular Disease Across Population and EHR Data
summary: This research introduces CardioMeta, a calibrated multi-task prediction model for diabetes, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease using both population and Electronic Health Record (EHR) data. It aims to improve early detection and prevention of cardiometabolic diseases.

title: Learning Faster without Deeper Networks: A*-Inspired Batch Selection for Efficient CNN Training
summary: This research proposes an A*-inspired batch selection method for Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) training, aiming for faster learning without deeper networks. It addresses inefficiencies caused by random mini-batch shuffling.

title: Trainable Spline Representations for Physics-Informed Learning
summary: This work introduces Physics-Informed Splines (PI-Splines), a structured spline-based architecture for physics-informed learning. It directly parametrizes unknown fields through tensor-product B-splines instead of neural networks.

title: CoG-Guided Weight Correction for Fault-Tolerant Deep Neural Networks
summary: This paper proposes a Center of Gravity (CoG) guided weight correction method for fault-tolerant Deep Neural Networks. It aims to restore faulty weights to improve reliability in safety-critical applications vulnerable to hardware and memory faults.

title: From Diffusion to Reaction-Diffusion: A Dynamical-Systems View of Oversmoothing in Hypergraph Neural Networks
summary: This research investigates oversmoothing in Hypergraph Neural Networks from a dynamical-systems perspective, linking it to representation collapse due to strong multi-way feature mixing. It explores the dynamics of higher-order couplings.

title: Scaling Time Series Classification via XAI-Driven Data Reduction
summary: This paper introduces drXAI, a novel methodology that repurposes Explainable AI (XAI) attribution methods for data reduction to improve time series classification performance. It explores the practical utility of XAI in downstream tasks.

title: AquaAugmentor: A Novel Feature Augmentation Algorithm for Water Potability Prediction
summary: This paper proposes AquaAugmentor, a novel feature augmentation algorithm designed to improve the accuracy of water potability prediction. It addresses challenges with complex and variable water source data.

title: Knowledge-Assisted Multi-Graph Dependency Learning for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection in Multi-Stage Industrial Processes
summary: This paper introduces a knowledge-assisted multi-graph dependency learning method for multivariate time series anomaly detection in complex, multi-stage industrial processes. It focuses on effectively monitoring and detecting anomalies in interdependent sensor data.

title: QUADS: Stabilizing NVFP4 Reinforcement Learning for MoE via QUantization-error Alignment across Dual Sides
summary: This paper introduces QUADS, a method for stabilizing NVFP4 reinforcement learning in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Large Language Models by aligning quantization errors. It aims to accelerate rollout generation using low-precision formats.

title: Graph Coloring Approach to Solving Sudoku with Oscillatory Neural Networks
summary: This paper proposes an Oscillatory Neural Network (ONN)-based solver for Sudoku, leveraging a graph coloring approach. It explores the application of physics-based computing paradigms to constrained combinatorial problems.

title: In-context learning of closed form solution to simple linear regression task using transformer with linear self-attention
summary: This paper investigates in-context learning in transformers with linear self-attention, demonstrating their capability to derive closed-form solutions for simple linear regression tasks. It explores how transformers implement solvers for such problems.

title: ContinuityBench: A Benchmark and Systems Study of Stateful Failover in Multi-Provider LLM Routing
summary: This paper introduces ContinuityBench, a new benchmark and systems study focused on evaluating stateful failover mechanisms in multi-provider LLM routing. It aims to address conversational continuity challenges in production LLM deployments during outages.

title: (MPO)$^2$: Multivariate Polynomial Optimization based on Matrix Product Operators
summary: This paper introduces (MPO)^2, a method for multivariate polynomial optimization based on Matrix Product Operators, aimed at universal function approximation in machine learning and signal processing. It offers a way to express complex input-output relationships.

title: Knowledge-Guided Cross-Modal Fusion for Adult-to-Pediatric ECG Transfer via Label-Conditioned Contrastive Alignment
summary: This paper proposes a knowledge-guided cross-modal fusion method for transferring ECG interpretation models from adult to pediatric populations. It uses label-conditioned contrastive alignment to improve model performance when pediatric labels are scarce.

title: An Exploratory Study of Single Channel Surface Electromyography for Hand Gesture Classification
summary: This exploratory study investigates the feasibility of classifying ten hand gestures using single-channel surface electromyography (sEMG). It aims to enable practical deployment in low-power and embedded systems by reducing reliance on multichannel sensors.

title: Presentation, Not Mechanism: A Render Confound in Deprecation-Aware Memory Evaluation
summary: This paper highlights a render confound in deprecation-aware memory evaluation for AI systems, addressing challenges in retrieving and discerning currently valid information from constantly revising records. It focuses on how AI systems recall information over time.

title: Constrained Hebbian Learning Supports Efficient Representational Allocation under Structural Constraints
summary: This paper investigates how constrained Hebbian learning supports efficient representational allocation in neural networks under structural constraints, drawing inspiration from biological systems. It explores how neural codes compress information given biological limitations.

title: CLaC@FinMMEval 2026 Task 3: Sentiment-Augmented Deep Reinforcement Learning for Active Trading -- An Alpha-Reward Approach
summary: This paper presents a system for active trading using sentiment-augmented deep reinforcement learning, designed for daily trading decisions for assets like Bitcoin and Tesla. It formulates the problem as a discrete-action Markov Decision Process.

title: Revisiting data-driven dynamic security assessment with a tabular foundation model
summary: This paper revisits data-driven dynamic security assessment (DSA) for power systems by proposing a tabular foundation model approach. It aims to overcome limitations of existing machine learning methods that require extensive labeled data.

title: DELUGE: Towards Continental-Scale Daily Pluvial Flood Damage Prediction via Interpretable Conditioning on Foundation Model Embeddings
summary: This paper introduces DELUGE, a method for continental-scale daily pluvial flood damage prediction using interpretable conditioning on foundation model embeddings. It aims to improve prediction accuracy for rainfall-driven flooding.

title: When Model Merging Rivals Joint Multi-Task Reinforcement Learning: A Task-Vector Geometry Analysis
summary: This paper conducts a task-vector geometry analysis to investigate when model merging rivals joint multi-task reinforcement learning. It evaluates model merging as a substitute for multi-task training in RL settings.

title: Physics-Based Deep Spatiotemporal Hyperlocal Radar Nowcasting with a Multi-Variable U-Net for High-Resolution Precipitation Forecasting
summary: This paper introduces a physics-based deep spatiotemporal hyperlocal radar nowcasting method using a multi-variable U-Net for high-resolution precipitation forecasting. It aims to improve short-range weather prediction for flood management.

title: Neural spectroscopy of AlphaFold2 reveals encoded protein conformational landscapes
summary: This paper proposes "neural spectroscopy" to analyze AlphaFold2, revealing its encoded protein conformational landscapes. It treats AlphaFold2 not just as a prediction tool but as a scientific object for deeper analysis of protein structure.

title: DADiff: Diffusion-Driven Cross-Domain Policy Adaptation for Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper introduces DADiff, a diffusion-driven method for cross-domain policy adaptation in reinforcement learning. It addresses the challenge of transferring policies between domains with differing dynamics through online dynamics adaptation.

title: VarRate: Training-Free Variable-Rate KV Cache Compression for Long-Context LLMs
summary: This paper introduces VarRate, a training-free variable-rate KV cache compression method designed to alleviate the memory bottleneck in long-context large language model (LLM) inference. It optimizes how LLMs store and recall information within their context window.

title: EpiNarrate: Agentic Generation of Grounded Narratives from Epidemiological Scenario Projections
summary: This paper introduces EpiNarrate, an agentic system designed to generate clear and accessible public health narratives from complex epidemiological projections. It aims to communicate contextualized and quantitatively grounded insights to policymakers and the public.

title: SkillCorpus: Consolidating and Evaluating the Open Skill Ecosystem for Real-World LLM Agents
summary: SkillCorpus is a new resource for consolidating and evaluating the open skill ecosystem for real-world LLM agents, which are popular for extending agent capabilities. It addresses the fragmentation, redundancy, and uneven quality of existing agent skill repositories.

title: Adaptive Multi-Step Lookahead Decoding for Diffusion Language Models
summary: This research introduces an adaptive multi-step lookahead decoding method for masked diffusion language models (DLMs), which enables parallel text generation. The method aims to improve the accuracy-efficiency trade-off by exploring future decoding states before committing.

title: Better Starts, Better Ends: Bootstrapped Iterative Self-Reasoning Distillation for Compressed Reasoning
summary: This paper proposes a bootstrapped iterative self-reasoning distillation method to improve the efficiency of large reasoning models by compressing their chain-of-thought traces. The goal is to reduce redundant computations and improve the final answer without sacrificing performance.

title: Before the Action: Benchmarking LLMs on Prospective Hypothesis Discovery
summary: This paper introduces Prospective Hypothesis Discovery (PHD), a new benchmark designed to measure Large Language Models' (LLMs) ability to navigate the open-ended, pre-conclusion stage of scientific discovery. It assesses models' capacity to autonomously construct grounded and discriminative hypotheses.

title: Cost-efficient generative AI summarization for scalable automated essay scoring in educational assessment
summary: This study proposes a generative AI-assisted summarization framework to improve automated essay scoring (AES) in educational assessment by overcoming transformer input-length limitations for long essays. The goal is to enable cost-efficient and scalable assessment.

title: CAMMAR: Culture-Aware Matryoshka for Metaphorical Arabic Representations
summary: CAMMAR introduces a "Culture-Aware Matryoshka" approach to improve metaphorical Arabic representations in language models, which currently struggle to capture culturally grounded meaning. The method aims to better distinguish lexical, cultural, and metaphorical information.

title: Conditional Reliability of Toxicity Signals for Multilingual and Code-Mixed Abuse Detection
summary: This research investigates the conditional reliability of toxicity signals for multilingual and code-mixed abuse detection, particularly in Indian short texts. It highlights that existing moderation tools are unreliable under code-mixing, transliteration, slang, and language mismatch.

title: An MLIR-Based Compilation Method for Large Language Models
summary: This paper proposes an MLIR-based compilation method addressing challenges in deploying Large Language Models (LLMs) on specialized AI accelerators. It focuses on importing trained models into compiler-friendly intermediate representations and efficiently scheduling autoregressive operations.

title: How Much Human Label Variation Does Formal Semantic Structure Explain?: Group-Level Effects and Item-Level Ceilings in NLI
summary: This research investigates how much human label variation in natural language inference (NLI) can be explained by formal semantic structure. It measures this using a rule-based operator and monotonicity tagging on SNLI and MNLI datasets.

title: Induction in Both Directions: A Mechanistic Analysis of In-Context Learning in Masked Diffusion Language Models
summary: This work provides a mechanistic analysis of in-context learning in Masked Diffusion Language Models (DLMs), an alternative to autoregressive transformers. It studies how DLMs implement induction, a key mechanism behind in-context learning.

title: From Plausible to Actionable: A Position on LLM Self-Explanations
summary: This paper discusses Large Language Model (LLM) self-explanations, where models generate natural language rationales for their decisions, as a promising direction for explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). It explores how these explanations can move from plausible to actionable.

title: BayesPO: Bayesian Prompt Optimization via Parallel-Tempered Gradient-Guided Discrete MCMC
summary: BayesPO introduces a novel prompt optimization method for large language models (LLMs) that uses Bayesian posterior sampling over discrete prompt tokens. This approach aims to adapt LLMs efficiently without updating model parameters, improving their performance.

title: Candidate Attended Dialogue State Tracking Using BERT
summary: This paper proposes a candidate-attended dialogue state tracking (DST) method using BERT as a core component in task-oriented dialogue systems. DST aims to estimate the user belief or dialogue state at each turn of a conversation.

title: Loop the Loopies!
summary: This paper introduces Loopie, a new series of looped Transformer Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models. The series includes a 20B-parameter model with 2B active parameters and a 6B-parameter model with 0.6B active parameters, presented as the most powerful looped Transformer to date.

title: Frontier AI performance across the business disciplines: a case-grounded benchmark of knowledge work and analytical reasoning
summary: This paper introduces a new case-grounded benchmark designed to assess frontier AI performance across business disciplines, focusing on knowledge work and analytical reasoning. It aims to measure AI progress beyond capabilities like factual recall or narrow question answering.

title: Frontier Language Models Struggle to Copy: Text Can Be Better Viewed in 2D
summary: This research demonstrates that frontier language models struggle with the simple operation of exactly copying an input string, attributing this failure to positional encodings in Transformers. It suggests that text might be better viewed in 2D to address this limitation.

title: Controlling Implicit Shortcut Reliance in L2 Spoken English Auto-markers
summary: This research focuses on controlling implicit shortcut reliance in L2 spoken English auto-markers within speech and language processing tasks. It addresses issues of fairness and robustness in these systems by mitigating unintended biases.

title: Rate-Utility Frontiers for Language Encodings: Comparing Tokens, Bytes, and Pixels Under Controlled Linguistic Content
summary: This research compares different language encodings (tokens, bytes, and pixels) for language models under controlled linguistic content. It aims to establish rate-utility frontiers to understand what each encoding preserves for diverse languages.

title: ToolSciVer: Multimodal Scientific Claim Verification with Visual Tool Augmented Reinforcement Learning
summary: ToolSciVer introduces a new method for Multimodal Scientific Claim Verification (MSCV) that uses visual tool augmented reinforcement learning. This approach aims to verify scientific claims by effectively locating decisive visual evidence from papers, including figures, tables, and text.

title: Hidden in Thought: Transferable Chain-of-Thought Artifacts Induce Harmful Behavior
summary: This research investigates how harmful chain-of-thought (CoT) artifacts from compromised language models can transfer unsafe behavior and be used for reusable jailbreak attacks. It examines emergent-misalignment and refusal-ablated organisms to transplant harmful CoTs.

title: AI Watermark Evidence Fails Forensic Readiness: An Empirical Evaluation
summary: This paper empirically evaluates the forensic readiness of AI watermarks, concluding that their reliability is insufficient despite increasing government mandates like the EU AI Act and California's SB 942. It questions whether current watermarking can meet legal requirements for robustness and permanence.

title: HCIG: A Hierarchical Cross-Modal Incongruity Graph Network for Multimodal Sarcasm and Cyberbullying Detection
summary: This paper introduces HCIG, a Hierarchical Cross-Modal Incongruity Graph Network, designed for improved multimodal sarcasm and cyberbullying detection. The model addresses challenges by analyzing incongruity between textual and visual information.

title: Understanding Reasoning from Pretraining to Post-Training
summary: This research investigates the impact of pretraining choices and reinforcement learning post-training on the reasoning capabilities of large language models. It seeks to understand how these stages contribute to solving complex reasoning tasks.

title: An Exam for Active Observers
summary: This paper examines whether multimodal large language models (M-LLMs) demonstrate active observation, a characteristic of human vision where gaze is continuously redirected by intermediate hypotheses. It explores the cognitive capabilities of M-LLMs in perception.

title: Learn to Memorize: Scalable Continual Learning in Semiparametric Models with Mixture-of-Neighbors Induction Memory
summary: This research introduces "Mixture-of-Neighbors Induction Memory," a novel approach for scalable continual learning in semiparametric language models. It aims to integrate learning capabilities into the non-parametric memory component of these models.

title: Decoupled Alignment for Robust Plug-and-Play Adaptation
summary: This paper introduces Decoupled Alignment, a training-free safety enhancement method for robustly aligning large language models (LLMs). It prevents "shadow alignment" when models are adapted, offering a plug-and-play approach for safety.

title: Latent Fusion Jailbreak: Blending Harmful and Harmless Representations to Elicit Unsafe LLM Outputs
summary: This paper presents the Latent Fusion Jailbreak (LFJ), a technique that manipulates internal representations of safety-aligned large language models to elicit unsafe outputs. It blends harmful and harmless representations to circumvent safety mechanisms.

title: Analysing Moral Bias in Finetuned LLMs through Mechanistic Interpretability
summary: This research analyzes moral bias, specifically the Knobe effect, in finetuned large language models using mechanistic interpretability. It aims to clarify the mechanisms through which these biases manifest in AI systems.

title: Bifocal Attention: Harmonizing Geometric and Spectral Positional Embeddings for Algorithmic Generalization
summary: This paper introduces Bifocal Attention, a method designed to harmonize geometric and spectral positional embeddings in large language models. It aims to improve algorithmic generalization by addressing limitations like "Spectral Rigidity" in standard RoPE.

title: Large-Scale Terminal Agentic Trajectory Generation from Dockerized Environments
summary: This research focuses on generating large-scale terminal agentic trajectories from Dockerized environments, crucial for training agentic models for terminal-based tasks. It addresses challenges in creating high-quality, executable, and reproducible data.

title: Speculative Decoding with a Speculative Vocabulary
summary: This paper introduces "Speculative Decoding with a Speculative Vocabulary," a novel approach designed to accelerate language model inference. It builds upon existing speculative decoding methods to offer substantial speedups while maintaining identical outputs.

title: KDFlow: A User-Friendly and Efficient Knowledge Distillation Framework for Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces KDFlow, a user-friendly and efficient knowledge distillation framework designed to compress large language models (LLMs) into smaller, more performant versions. It aims to improve efficiency despite the distinct roles of student and teacher models.

title: When Perplexity Lies: Generation-Focused Distillation of Hybrid Sequence Models
summary: This research proposes a "generation-focused distillation" approach for hybrid sequence models, addressing issues where perplexity can be misleading for evaluating generative quality. The method aims to reduce inference costs while achieving high-quality generation.

title: Robust Explanations for User Trust in Enterprise NLP Systems
summary: This paper emphasizes the necessity of robust explanations for fostering user trust in enterprise NLP systems, particularly in black-box deployments. It highlights the difficulties in pre-deployment validation for explainers.

title: Brain-CLIPLM: Semantic Compression for EEG-to-Text Decoding
summary: This paper introduces Brain-CLIPLM, a method utilizing semantic compression to enhance the decoding of natural language from non-invasive electroencephalography (EEG) signals. It addresses challenges related to low signal-to-noise ratio and limited information bandwidth.

title: RLearner-LLM: Balancing Logical Grounding and Fluency in Large Language Models via Hybrid Direct Preference Optimization
summary: This paper introduces RLearner-LLM, a method that employs Hybrid Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) to balance logical grounding and fluency in large language models. It aims to overcome the verbosity bias found in standard DPO approaches for knowledge-intensive generation.

title: From Articles to Premises: Building PrimeFacts, an Extraction Methodology and Resource for Fact-Checking Evidence
summary: This paper introduces PrimeFacts, a methodology and resource designed for extracting fine-grained evidence from full fact-checking articles. It aims to make rich supporting evidence accessible for automated verification systems.

title: VCG-Bench: Towards A Unified Visual-Centric Benchmark for Structured Generation and Editing
summary: This paper proposes VCG-Bench, a new unified visual-centric benchmark designed to evaluate vision-language models on structured generation and editing tasks. It aims to address a critical gap in assessing VLM capabilities for professional workflows.

title: Probing LLMs for Syntactic Structure Beyond Universal Dependencies: A Minimalist Phase Account in English
summary: This research probes large language models (LLMs) to determine if they encode syntactic distinctions beyond those found in Universal Dependencies. It uses structural probes and English wh-movement stimuli to analyze their internal linguistic representations.

title: What Should a Skill Remember? Quality--Cost Trade-offs in Cost-Aware Skill Rewriting for Language Model Agents
summary: This paper investigates the trade-offs between the quality and cost of skills for large language model agents, specifically focusing on skill rewriting. It explores how shorter skills can sometimes increase agent expenses by removing valuable information.

title: It Takes One to Bias Them All: Breaking Bad with One-Shot GRPO
summary: This paper investigates how easily the safety guardrails of large language models, typically set by post-training alignment, can be broken. It demonstrates that one-shot Group Relative Policy Optimization can cause LLMs to generate toxic and offensive statements.

title: AuAu: A Benchmark for Auditing Authoritarian Alignment in Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces AuAu, a comprehensive benchmark designed to assess the risk of large language models exhibiting or promoting authoritarian attitudes. The benchmark aims to audit the authoritarian alignment of LLMs given their increasing role in daily life.

title: An expressivity analysis of hierarchical modelling in deep transformers via bounded-depth grammars
summary: This research analyzes the expressivity of hierarchical modeling in deep transformers using bounded-depth grammars. It investigates how transformers, a dominant architecture in language modeling, derive their power from forming hierarchical representations.

title: What Models Express, Suppress, and Resist: Auditing Open-Weight LLMs with Persona Vectors
summary: This paper introduces 'persona vectors' as a method for auditing open-weight large language models to understand their expressed, suppressed, and resisted behaviors. These vectors act as behavioral directions in activation space, revealing insights not apparent through prompting alone.

title: LLM-as-a-Judge Scores Are Unreliable Optimization Signals in Closed-Loop Table Recognition
summary: This research finds that LLM-as-a-Judge scores are unreliable optimization signals when used in closed-loop table recognition, despite their widespread use for feedback. The study uses deterministic TEDS evaluation on FinTabNet and OmniDocBench datasets to validate this finding.

title: An Empirical Study of Handcrafted Feature Learning and Convolutional Neural Networks for Facial Expression Recognition
summary: This empirical study compares handcrafted feature learning with convolutional neural networks for facial expression recognition, a key computer vision task. It examines the performance of both approaches for applications like human-computer interaction and mental health monitoring.

title: Rethinking the Readout: Unlocking Video Backbones for AI-Generated Video Detection
summary: This research explores using video-pretrained backbones to improve the detection of AI-generated videos, focusing on capturing subtle temporal artifacts and inter-frame inconsistencies. It aims to develop more effective methods for identifying synthetic video content.

title: Training-Free Open-Vocabulary 3D Point-Cloud Segmentation on the Generalized Few-Shot Benchmark
summary: This paper proposes a training-free, open-vocabulary method for 3D point-cloud segmentation on the generalized few-shot benchmark. It aims to segment scenes into both seen base classes and novel classes by reconciling 3D vision-language priors with few-shot support.

title: Reasoning-Guided Part-Level Visual Grounding via Reinforcement Learning
summary: This research proposes a reasoning-guided method for part-level visual grounding in multimodal large language models using reinforcement learning. It addresses the struggle of MLLMs to ground specific object parts due to a missing object-part hierarchy.

title: GS-RealBlur: A Flexible Data Acquisition Framework for Real-World Image Deblurring
summary: This paper introduces GS-RealBlur, a flexible data acquisition framework designed to generate high-quality, large-scale paired data for training learning-based image deblurring models. It aims to overcome the limitations of synthetic data and complex real-world capture systems.

title: Dataset-Origin Signatures and Shortcut Learning in Screening Mammography AI: A Cross-Dataset Case Study
summary: This cross-dataset case study investigates dataset-origin signatures and shortcut learning in AI for screening mammography. It examines how training data composition impacts model reliability and performance in medical image analysis.

title: Trajectory-aware Cross-view Geo-localization with Sequential Observations
summary: This research presents a trajectory-aware method for cross-view geo-localization using sequential observations, matching ground-level data with satellite imagery. It aims to leverage richer spatiotemporal cues from trajectories, beyond single images or video clips.

title: Intentional Electromagnetic Interference Attacks on Facial Recognition
summary: This research investigates intentional electromagnetic interference attacks as a physical method to target facial recognition systems. It explores the vulnerability of biometric AI to non-digital, physical presentation attacks.

title: Physics-aware Masked Diffusion-based Flood Simulation for Urban Fisheye Disaster Detection
summary: This paper introduces a physics-aware masked diffusion-based flood simulation method for urban fisheye disaster detection. It addresses the data shortage for climate-related flooding by creating anomaly detection models through simulations.

title: ImprovedVBGS: Real-time Continual Variational Bayes Gaussian Splatting
summary: This paper presents ImprovedVBGS, a real-time continual variational Bayes Gaussian Splatting method for on-the-fly 3D reconstruction. It enables continual learning without replay buffers using Coordinate Ascent Variational Inference, benefiting applications in robotics and autonomous navigation.

title: When Can Test-Time Adaptation Help Zero-Shot CT Vision-Language Models?
summary: This paper investigates when test-time adaptation improves zero-shot 3D CT vision-language models for classifying abnormalities from text prompts, enabling deployment in label-scarce clinical settings.

title: Are All Tokens Necessary for Visual Place Recognition? An Empirical Study of Token Reduction for Efficient Inference
summary: This empirical study investigates token reduction methods for visual place recognition (VPR) using vision transformers, aiming to improve computational efficiency by addressing the overhead of processing all visual tokens during inference.

title: Geometric Distillation from Rectified Stereo: Leveraging Epipolar Cues for Monocular Depth
summary: This paper proposes geometric distillation from rectified stereo, a method leveraging epipolar cues to address the scale ambiguity limitation of monocular depth foundation models in metric depth estimation across diverse environments.

title: WREN: Low Light Image Enhancement Using Retinex theory-based Double U-Net-like Structures
summary: This paper proposes WREN, a new neural network based on Retinex theory and double U-Net-like structures, designed for robust low-light image enhancement across various dynamic range scenes.

title: Benchmarking MRI Representations for Deep Learning-Based Focal Cortical Dysplasia Segmentation
summary: This research focuses on benchmarking different MRI representations for deep learning models, aiming to improve the challenging task of focal cortical dysplasia segmentation in drug-resistant epilepsy.

title: Region-Grounded Vision-Language Learning for Detection-Guided Mammographic Lesion Classification
summary: This paper introduces region-grounded vision-language learning as a method to improve mammographic lesion classification by adapting vision-language models for localized lesions, addressing limitations of global image-text alignment.

title: StructGen: Disambiguating Multi-Reference Image Generation via Structured Context Modeling
summary: This paper introduces StructGen, a method that uses structured context modeling to disambiguate multi-reference image generation, enabling more accurate integration of attributes from multiple reference images under textual instructions.

title: BCG-Former: Toward Pareto-Efficient Hyperspectral Image Classification via Band-Contextual Gating
summary: This paper introduces BCG-Former, a new model designed for Pareto-efficient hyperspectral image classification, optimizing for both accuracy and computational constraints for deployment on platforms with strict budgets.

title: DiTango: Cost-Effective Parallel Diffusion Generation with Selective Attention State Reuse
summary: This paper presents DiTango, a method for cost-effective parallel diffusion generation using selective attention state reuse, designed to address scalability challenges in Diffusion Transformers for high-resolution content creation.

title: Model Merging for Medical LVLMs: A Benchmark and a Winner-Take-All Approach
summary: This paper introduces a benchmark and a winner-take-all approach for model merging in medical large vision-language models, addressing the adaptation of LVLMs for specialized medical imaging tasks.

title: PE-Field 4D: Video Generation Models as Canvas
summary: This paper introduces PE-Field 4D, which revisits the role of positional encoding in video diffusion transformers to improve control over scene geometry under viewpoint changes and camera motion for video generation models.

title: Efficient Frame Selection for Long Videos at Test Time with Attention-Based MLLM Selectors
summary: This paper proposes a method for efficient frame selection using attention-based MLLM selectors, enabling multimodal large language models to better understand long videos by intelligently choosing relevant frames at test time.

title: GoStop: Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Temporal Aggregation in Event-Based Feature Tracking
summary: This paper introduces GoStop, a reinforcement learning method for adaptive temporal aggregation, designed to improve event-based feature tracking for robust perception in dynamic environments.

title: Efficient Difficulty-Aware Dynamic Routing for Diffusion-Based Real-World Image Super-Resolution
summary: This paper proposes an efficient difficulty-aware dynamic routing method to improve diffusion-based models for real-world image super-resolution, addressing current limitations in stable diffusion approaches.

title: Per-Stroke Temporal Control for Text-to-Motion via Action Units and Action-Detection Guidance
summary: This paper introduces Action Units (AUs) for per-stroke temporal control in text-to-motion models, aiming to improve the reliability of generating individual actions and their timing based on textual prompts.

title: Event3R: Asynchronous-to-Global 3D Reconstruction from Event Camera via Spatial-Temporal Feature Aggregation
summary: This paper presents Event3R, a new method for asynchronous-to-global 3D reconstruction from event camera data, utilizing spatial-temporal feature aggregation to achieve robust 3D reconstruction.

title: IoUPD: IoU-Aware Privileged Distillation for Visual Grounding with Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces IoUPD, an IoU-aware privileged distillation method designed to improve visual grounding capabilities in multimodal large language models by enhancing bounding-box coordinate generation.

title: Debiasing Text-to-Image Evaluation via Implicit Cultural Alignment Reward Modeling
summary: This paper proposes implicit cultural alignment reward modeling to debias text-to-image evaluation, aiming to improve the assessment of cultural authenticity for fair and trustworthy generative AI.

title: Personalized Image Aesthetic Assessment via Preference-rich Sample Mining and Cohort Merging
summary: This paper proposes a method for personalized image aesthetic assessment (PIAA) using preference-rich sample mining and cohort merging, aiming to predict individual-specific aesthetic ratings for images.

title: GeoChrono: Benchmarking and Rethinking Long-Term Temporal Understanding in Remote Sensing
summary: This paper introduces GeoChrono, a new benchmark and framework for rethinking long-term temporal understanding in remote sensing, focusing on models' ability to track changes and reason across time and space.

title: SlotMem: Character-Addressable Internal Memory for Narrative Long Video Generation
summary: This paper introduces SlotMem, an internal memory mechanism designed for narrative long video generation to maintain consistent character identities across scenes and temporal gaps. It addresses the challenge of retrieving memory using cues not aligned with character identity preservation.

title: Modularized Dynamic-Granularity Video LLM for Multi-Event Long Video Understanding
summary: This paper proposes a modularized dynamic-granularity Video LLM designed to improve multi-event long video understanding by addressing the limitations of visual token budgets. It aims to better capture multiple key events in extended video sequences.

title: Multimodal Ambivalence and Hesitancy Recognition via Cross-Attention and Gated Fusion
summary: This research presents a multimodal framework utilizing cross-attention and gated fusion for recognizing ambivalence and hesitancy in video, developed for the ABAW11 challenge. It fuses textual, acoustic, and visual modalities using pretrained encoders like F2LLM-v2-0.6B.

title: On the Geometry of Learned Representations in Event-Based Multi-Modal Egomotion Estimation
summary: This paper investigates the geometry of learned representations in event-based multi-modal egomotion estimation, contrasting with classical geometric optimization frameworks. The work explores how modern AI approaches handle motion inversion and other estimation tasks.

title: Test-Time Noise Guided Adaptation for Realistic Autoregressive Video Generation
summary: This paper proposes a test-time noise guided adaptation method to address error accumulation in autoregressive video diffusion models, enabling more realistic generation of arbitrarily long videos. The approach aims to prevent the denoised sequence from drifting from conditioning.

title: Von Mises-Fisher Mixture Model with Dynamic Shrinkage for Realistic Test-Time Transduction
summary: This paper introduces a Von Mises-Fisher Mixture Model with Dynamic Shrinkage to improve the performance of vision-language models during test-time transduction. The method is designed to address challenges posed by highly imbalanced class distributions in realistic evaluations.

title: EgoExoMoCap: Distributed Ego-Exo Human Motion Capture
summary: This research presents EgoExoMoCap, a distributed system for human motion capture from head-mounted devices that combines egocentric and exocentric tracking. It offers a scalable way to acquire real-world human motion data crucial for embodied AI and VR/AR applications.

title: Hardware-triggered Time Synchronization of Roadside Multi-lidar, Multi-camera Measurement System for Accurate Data Alignment
summary: This paper presents an open-source, hardware-triggered time-synchronization circuit for roadside multi-lidar, multi-camera measurement systems to achieve accurate data alignment. This aims to improve reliable environment perception, particularly in dense urban traffic scenarios.

title: Exo2EgoPose: Leveraging Exocentric Demonstrations for Vision-Language guided Egocentric 3D Hand Pose Forecasting
summary: This research introduces Exo2EgoPose, a method that leverages exocentric demonstrations and vision-language guidance for egocentric 3D hand pose forecasting. It aims to improve multimodal perception and fine-grained action prediction for applications like robot manipulation.

title: Orbis 2: A Hierarchical World Model for Driving
summary: This paper introduces Orbis 2, a hierarchical world model for driving that factorizes future prediction to enhance spatial reasoning and semantic understanding. It aims to overcome limitations of single-level world models in real-world downstream tasks.

title: Handwritten and Printed Text Segmentation via Region-Aware Human-Writing Descriptor Engineering
summary: This research proposes a method for handwritten and printed text segmentation using region-aware human-writing descriptor engineering. It aims to improve accuracy in document digitization tasks where high computational cost deep learning models are often used.

title: More with Less: a Large Scale Remote Sensing VLM with a Simple Recipe
summary: This paper presents a large-scale remote sensing vision-language model, focusing on a simple recipe to achieve open-ended reasoning over Earth Observation data. It explores architectural designs to support a variety of remote sensing tasks.

title: Beyond Unfolding: 60x Faster One-Stage Unmixing for Closely-Spaced Infrared Small Targets
summary: This paper introduces a method for 60x faster one-stage unmixing for Closely-Spaced Infrared Small Targets (CSIST), addressing the challenge of energy overlap in infrared images. It aims to overcome the limitations of traditional detection methods for ambiguous targets.

title: DPNeXt: A Lightweight Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Framework for Efficient ViT-Based Multi-Task Dense Prediction
summary: This paper proposes DPNeXt, a lightweight multi-scale feature fusion framework for efficient ViT-based multi-task dense prediction in robotics perception systems. It integrates semantic segmentation and depth estimation using Vision Foundation Models.

title: Xiaomi-Robotics-1: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models with over 100K Hours of Real-World Trajectories
summary: This paper presents Xiaomi-Robotics-1, a foundational vision-language-action (VLA) model scaled with over 100K hours of real-world trajectories. It enables robots to perform diverse mobile manipulation tasks based on language instructions and adapt to novel downstream tasks.

title: NeuroCommitSSM: Decision-Centric Shared Autonomy for Safe Assistive Manipulation via EEG-EMG-ET Commit Readiness
summary: This paper introduces NeuroCommitSSM, a decision-centric framework for safe assistive robotic manipulation in shared autonomy, which predicts a commit-readiness score from synchronized EEG, EMG, and eye-tracking data. It models when to execute actions for safer human-robot collaboration.

title: Robust Silicone Pour Casting and Sensor Embedding Procedures for Soft Robotic Actuators
summary: This paper details robust silicone pour casting and sensor embedding procedures for the fabrication of soft robotic actuators. The methods aim to improve reproducible and scalable manufacturing of soft robots for real-world deployment.

title: Environment Design for Reliable Shared Autonomy with Probabilistic Guarantees
summary: This research investigates environment design to achieve reliable shared autonomy with probabilistic guarantees, where humans and robots collaboratively perform tasks. It focuses on how workspace design affects intent inference and overall system reliability.

title: PACE: Persona Adaptation through Conversational Elicitation in Human-Robot Interaction
summary: This paper presents PACE, a method for persona adaptation through conversational elicitation in human-robot interaction to equip humanoid robots with coherent and adaptable personas. This aims to foster more natural, engaging, and trustworthy interactions.

title: Scalable Open-Source Visuotactile Sensor for 6-Axis Contact Wrench Estimation in Tensegrity Robots
summary: This paper introduces a scalable, open-source visuotactile sensor designed for tensegrity robots, enabling six-axis contact wrench estimation and contact detection. The endcap sensor integrates an elastomeric shell, TPU interface, and rigid base.

title: Difference-Based Relational Learning for Zero-Shot Object-Goal Visual Navigation With Direct Sim-to-Real Transfer
summary: This research proposes a Temporal Difference-Relational Network (T-DRN) for robust zero-shot object-goal visual navigation, addressing the sim-to-real gap in deep reinforcement learning for robots.

title: Learning a System-Level Surrogate for Hydraulic Excavators: A Simulation-to-Real LSTM Approach
summary: This paper proposes a simulation-to-real framework using LSTM networks to develop a digital surrogate for autonomous hydraulic excavators, addressing challenges in real-world experimentation.

title: Continuously Stable Structure through Plastic Deformation
summary: This research explores methods to achieve continuously stable structures in soft robots and grippers, which often face stability challenges due to their inherent compliance.

title: A Generative Partially Specified Finite State Machine Approach to Complex Behaviour Planning
summary: This paper proposes a generative partially specified finite state machine approach for complex behavior planning in autonomous robots, integrating concepts from Large Language Models and Behavior Trees.

title: RAVEN: Reinforcement-Adaptive Visibility-Graph Planning for Robust Humanoid Navigation with Collision-Free MPC
summary: RAVEN is a reinforcement-adaptive visibility-graph planning system designed for robust humanoid navigation in dynamic environments, using model predictive control for collision-free trajectories.

title: Implicit Virtual Leader: Decentralized Vision-Only Relative Pose Estimation for Multi-Robot Formations
summary: This work introduces a decentralized, vision-only relative pose estimation method for multi-robot formations, addressing limitations of classical leader-follower control in GPS-denied environments.

title: AC-VLA: Robust Out-of-Distribution Action Execution via Compositional Learning
summary: AC-VLA proposes a compositional learning approach for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to improve robust out-of-distribution action execution in robotic manipulation tasks.

title: A Task-Space Receding Horizon Controller for Fast Collision Avoidance
summary: This paper presents a task-space receding horizon controller for fast collision avoidance in robotic manipulators, enabling quick reactions to unexpected obstacle motion.

title: Towards Artificial Nerves: Biomimetic Optical-Fiber Tactile Sensing for Robots
summary: This research introduces OptiTac, a biomimetic optical-fiber tactile sensor for robots that emulates human mechanoreceptor-to-nerve architecture to enable more dexterous manipulation.

title: SkillNav: Score-Level Skill Intervention for Zero-Shot Object Goal Navigation
summary: SkillNav proposes a score-level skill intervention method for Vision-Language Model (VLM) agents to improve zero-shot object-goal navigation by addressing issues like dead-end stalls and inefficient paths.

title: Dynamics-Aware Meta-Imitation for Generalization to Unseen Robotic Manipulation
summary: This paper introduces Dynamics-Aware Meta-Imitation to enhance robotic manipulation, allowing robots to generalize learned skills to unseen tasks despite data scarcity and environmental variations.

title: Learning Reach-Avoid Task with Reinforcement Learning: Vectorized Simulation and Benchmark
summary: This work explores deep reinforcement learning for the reach-avoid task in robotic arms, presenting a vectorized simulation and benchmark for evaluating DRL effectiveness.

title: Embodied Active Learning under Limited Annotation and Navigation Budget for Object Detection
summary: This paper investigates embodied active learning for robots to adapt computer vision object detectors to unknown environments under constraints of annotation and navigation budgets.

title: Data and Learning Where it Matters for Contact-Rich Manipulation
summary: This research investigates improving learned policies for contact-rich robotic manipulation by focusing data collection on critical interactions, addressing generalization limitations.

title: BayesContact: Uncertain Pose Estimation via Visuo-Tactile Proposals and Simulation-based Inference
summary: BayesContact proposes a method for uncertain pose estimation in contact-rich manipulation, combining visuo-tactile proposals and simulation-based inference to achieve higher accuracy.

title: VTLoc: Learning-based Tactile Contact Localization in Visual Point Clouds
summary: VTLoc presents a learning-based method for tactile contact localization in visual point clouds, integrating vision and touch modalities to enhance robotic perception and manipulation.

title: Vision-Language-Motion Maps: An Open-Vocabulary, Uncertainty-Aware, Queryable Motion Attribute for 3D Scene Maps
summary: Vision-Language-Motion Maps (VLMM) introduce open-vocabulary, uncertainty-aware, and queryable 3D scene maps for robots, allowing them to understand and respond to language queries about dynamic scene elements.

title: Handroid: Bridging Dexterous Hand and Humanoid
summary: Handroid is a new robotic embodiment that bridges dexterous hands and humanoid robots, enabling contact-rich manipulation and whole-body interaction in human-centered environments.

title: PIXIE: A Zero-Shot texture-invariant 6D pose estimation framework for unseen objects with assembly defects
summary: PIXIE is a zero-shot, texture-invariant framework for 6D pose estimation of unseen objects with assembly defects, addressing a key challenge in robotics and industrial computer vision.

title: On the Use of AI-Driven Immersive Digital Technologies for Designing and Operating UAVs
summary: This paper explores the use of AI-driven immersive digital technologies to improve the design and operation of Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), addressing challenges in their modeling and control.

title: ContactFusion: Stochastic Poisson Surface Maps from Visual and Contact Sensing
summary: This paper proposes ContactFusion, a method combining visual and contact sensing with global mapping for precise robotic assembly, aiming to overcome noise in scene understanding.

title: Holistic Fusion: Task- and Setup-Agnostic Robot Localization and State Estimation with Factor Graphs
summary: This work introduces a flexible open-source solution using factor graphs for task- and setup-agnostic robot localization and state estimation, crucial for mobile robots operating in challenging environments.

title: SLAC: Safe and Efficient Real-Robot Reinforcement Learning via Unsupervised Simulation Pre-Training
summary: This research presents SLAC, a method for safe and efficient reinforcement learning in real robots, leveraging unsupervised simulation pre-training to control high-degree-of-freedom systems like mobile manipulators.

title: Sym2Real: Symbolic Dynamics with Residual Learning for Data-Efficient Adaptive Control
summary: Sym2Real is introduced as a data-driven framework for highly data-efficient adaptive control of low-level controllers, addressing the limitations of symbolic regression in real-world applications due to noise sensitivity.

title: A Systematic Study of Large Language Models for Task and Motion Planning With PDDLStream
summary: This study investigates the capabilities of large language models (LLMs) for task and motion planning in robotics, proposing an integration of LLM semantic knowledge with formal reasoning systems like PDDLStream.

title: Simultaneous Calibration of Noise Covariance and Kinematics for State Estimation of Legged Robots via Bi-level Optimization
summary: This work proposes a bi-level optimization framework for simultaneous calibration of noise covariance and kinematics, critical for accurate state estimation in legged and aerial robots operating in dynamic environments.

title: Human-Inspired Neuro-Symbolic World Modeling and Logic Reasoning for Interpretable Safe UAV Landing Site Assessment
summary: This paper explores a human-inspired neuro-symbolic world modeling and logic reasoning approach for interpretable and safe UAV landing site assessment in unstructured environments.

title: EmbodiedDiffusion: End-to-End Traversability-Guided Visual Diffusion for Heterogeneous Robot Navigation
summary: EmbodiedDiffusion is presented as an end-to-end traversability-guided visual diffusion method for heterogeneous robot navigation, aiming to simplify autonomous navigation by integrating traversability with trajectory planning.

title: Robust and Efficient MuJoCo-based Model Predictive Control via Web of Affine Spaces Derivatives
summary: This research proposes a robust and efficient Model Predictive Control (MPC) method using MuJoCo simulations via Web of Affine Spaces Derivatives, improving real-time control policies in robotics.

title: Passive Phase-Oriented Impedance Shaping for Rapid Acceleration in Soft Robotic Swimmers
summary: This work investigates constrained-layer damping (CLD) for passive phase-oriented impedance shaping, enabling rapid acceleration and burst maneuvers in soft robotic swimmers.

title: Interaction-Aware Whole-Body Control for Compliant Object Transport
summary: This paper proposes a bio-inspired, interaction-aware whole-body control method for assistive humanoids to perform compliant object transport in unstructured environments, addressing challenges with time-varying interaction forces.

title: MuxGel: Simultaneous Dual-Modal Visuo-Tactile Sensing via Spatially Multiplexing and Deep Reconstruction
summary: MuxGel is introduced as a spatially multiplexed visuo-tactile sensor that simultaneously captures external visual information and tactile data for precise robotic manipulation using deep reconstruction.

title: Troy Jackson poised to seize Maine baton after Platner's exit
summary: Democrats are rallying around former Maine Senate President Troy Jackson (D) in the quest to unseat Republican Sen. Susan Collins this fall after Graham Platner's embattled campaign crashed, burned and ended. Why it matters: Jackson's expected coronation is another win for the left flank of the Democratic party, which is lining up behind another progressive candidate as their best shot at flipping one of the most important seats to win back Senate control. Driving the news: Jackson all but locked up the nomination last weekend after Democrats across the state overwhelmingly selected his preferred delegate slate ahead of Saturday's convention. "We're well on our way to getting the government that we fucking deserve," Jackson said in a video to supporters. Top contenders in the crowded race have since ended their campaigns. Nirav Shah , Dan Kleban, and Jordan Wood all backed Jackson. The nominee will replace the scandal-plagued Platner, who was accused of sexual assault — an allegation he denies. Catch up quick: Jackson, whose campaign describes him as a fifth-generation logger and "lifelong fighter for workers' rights," finished third in June's Democratic primary for governor. His campaign priorities include passing Medicare for all, cutting off tax dollars to Israel's military, abolishing ICE and passing a federal right to abortion. Progressive kingmaker Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) endorsed Jackson in the gubernatorial race. What's next: Saturday's convention of 601 delegates from the state's 16 counties will make the new Democratic candidate official. "The convention will be fair, representative, and as transparent as possible as we all come together in service of our ultimate goal: defeat Susan Collins and win this Senate seat," Maine Democratic Party Chair Charlie Dingman said in a statement . Votes will be cast in rounds until one candidate reaches a majority, according to the party. The delegates are not pledged to any specific candidate, but a majority have reportedly committed to backing Jackson. Friction point: Jackson may glide through his party's nomination process, but Republicans have been preparing a massive ad blitz against Platner's replacement. summary: This research proposes "Weak-to-Strong Off-Policy RL via Auxiliary Branches," a reinforcement learning approach to enhance reasoning in large language models, addressing a critical bottleneck in existing policy optimization paradigms.

title: PPO-HSC: An Exploratory Reinforcement Learning Framework Based on Wide-Area Policy Coverage Optimization
summary: This paper introduces PPO-HSC, an exploratory reinforcement learning framework based on Wide-Area Policy Coverage Optimization, designed to mitigate mode collapse during large language model fine-tuning.

title: JUMP: Single-Pass Membership Inference on Fine-Tuned Diffusion Language Models
summary: This paper introduces JUMP, a single-pass membership inference attack designed to test whether a specific example was part of a fine-tuned discrete diffusion language model's training data.

title: ColGraphRAG: Late-Interaction Evidence Retrieval for Multimodal GraphRAG
summary: This paper introduces ColGraphRAG, a system for late-interaction evidence retrieval in multimodal GraphRAG, which organizes text, tables, and images into a structured evidence graph for question answering.

title: Shapley Context Pruning: A Cooperative Game Perspective for Context Reranking and Pruning
summary: This research proposes "Shapley Context Pruning," a cooperative game theory approach for context reranking and pruning to improve the efficiency of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems.

title: A Survey on the Verification of Reinforcement Learning Policies
summary: This survey paper reviews methods for verifying reinforcement learning policies, a critical area given the increasing application of RL in complex, safety-critical domains lacking rigorous behavioral guarantees for neural network-based policies.

title: Accurate and Efficient Long-Term Memory for LLM Agents
summary: This research focuses on developing accurate and efficient long-term memory systems for LLM agents, addressing limitations of existing approaches in preserving relational context for multi-hop and temporal reasoning.

title: Symbolic Augmentation Closes a Canonical-Equivalence Blind Spot in Neural Fact-Checkers
summary: This paper introduces symbolic augmentation to improve neural fact-checkers, addressing large language model hallucinations of numbers and units in scientific text by recasting error detection as typed verification and introducing a new taxonomy and benchmark.

title: SelKV: Selective KV Cache Merging with Per-Token Merge-or-Drop and Attention Compensation
summary: This paper introduces SelKV, a method for selective KV cache merging in large language models using per-token merge-or-drop and attention compensation, aiming to reduce the memory footprint caused by the KV cache.

title: RAIL Guard: Closing the Evaluation-to-Remediation Gap in Responsible AI for LLM Agents
summary: This paper introduces RAIL Guard, a closed-loop responsible AI pipeline designed for LLM agents, which evaluates and helps remediate unsafe content, aiming to close the gap between evaluation and remediation in existing guardrail systems.

title: Generalist AI Control: Towards Multi-purpose Adaptive Algorithms
summary: This research proposes a "Generalist Controller," a learning-based algorithm capable of controlling systems with varying orders and dynamics, moving towards multi-purpose adaptive algorithms in AI control.

title: LaCache: Exact Caching and Precision-Adaptive Inference for Diffusion Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces LaCache, a method for exact caching and precision-adaptive inference in Diffusion-based Large Language Models, aiming to reduce operator-level redundancy during parallel text generation.

title: Interactive Task Alignment as a POMDP
summary: This research models interactive task alignment, where language models must determine ambiguous user goals, as a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) to improve execution on real-world tasks.

title: When to Plan: Learning to Select Between Reactive Control and Deliberative Planning
summary: This paper studies meta-reasoning in artificial agents, focusing on how agents can learn to select between fast reactive control and slower deliberative planning, mirroring human cognitive abilities.

title: Berkeley and Heiserman as an Unexhausted Architecture for Embodied Machine Intelligence
summary: This paper explores the historical contributions of Edmund C. Berkeley and Heiserman, suggesting their work on symbolic logic and computing machinery offers an "unexhausted architecture" for embodied machine intelligence.

title: SEER: Supervised Learning to Control Energetic Reasoning
summary: This paper introduces SEER, a method utilizing supervised learning to control "energetic reasoning" within Constraint Programming, aiming to optimize the trade-off between search space reduction and computation time.

title: Nonuniformity Principle in Human-AI Coworking
summary: This paper introduces the Nonuniformity Principle, discussing the necessity of human judgment and oversight in multi-step AI-automated workflows to ensure output quality. It explores the practical aspects of human-AI coworking in generative AI applications.

title: From Modalities to Propositions: A Language-Centric Framework for Multimodal Intelligence
summary: This research proposes a language-centric framework for multimodal intelligence, representing diverse observations (image, video, text) as atomic propositions unified by a global semantic codebook. This method aims to improve multimodal data representation and understanding.

title: FST.ai 2.5: Explainable and Uncertainty-Aware AI for Olympic and Para-Taekwondo Decision Support, Athlete Digital Twins, and Federation-Scale Analytics
summary: This paper introduces FST.ai 2.5, an explainable and uncertainty-aware AI system designed for Olympic and Para-Taekwondo. It provides decision support, athlete digital twins, and federation-scale analytics for elite sports performance.

title: Just A Rather Very Intelligent Spoken Agent
summary: This paper introduces a "Spoken Agent" concept, aiming to improve user interaction with long-horizon AI agents by providing more transparent and dynamic updates in workflows. It addresses the current limitation of thin textual updates from AI agents.

title: A Research Prototype for Closed-Loop Generative Design of Customized Foot Orthoses via Semantic-Physics Alignment
summary: This research prototype explores a closed-loop generative design method for customized foot orthoses, addressing the semantic-physical misalignment between clinical prescriptions and 3D geometric parameters. It aims to automate the design process for patient-specific medical devices.

title: TopoTuner: Topological Finetuning of Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces TopoTuner, a novel topological fine-tuning method for Large Language Models that optimizes which pretrained components are trained during adaptation. It aims to provide a more efficient alternative to full fine-tuning and LoRA.

title: Diversity-Oriented Fine-Tuning for Uncertainty-Based Hallucination Detection
summary: This research proposes diversity-oriented fine-tuning strategies to enhance the detectability of hallucinations in Large Language Models. Unlike inference-stage methods, this approach modifies the model itself to improve uncertainty-based hallucination detection.

title: DS@GT ARC at eRisk 2026: Hybrid Multi-Agent LLM System with Structured Algorithmic Guidance for Conversational Depression Screening
summary: This describes a hybrid multi-agent LLM system with structured algorithmic guidance, developed for conversational depression screening as part of the eRisk 2026 Task 1 challenge. The system interviews LLM personas to assess depression profiles and BDI-II scores.

title: RECON: Benchmarking Agent Memory for Compositional Reasoning over Long Contexts
summary: This paper introduces RECON, a benchmark specifically designed to measure and evaluate the memory capabilities of LLM-based agents for compositional reasoning over long contexts. It focuses on agents' ability to retain, access, and reason with accumulated information.

title: Constraint-Anchored Reasoning Traces
summary: This research investigates error snowballing in autoregressive multimodal large language models (MLLMs) during chain-of-thought reasoning. It introduces "Constraint-Anchored Reasoning Traces" as a potential method to mitigate the cascading effect of early incorrect inferences.

title: Supporting Autonomous Process Execution within a Multi-Perspective Constraint Frame via Numeric Planning
summary: This paper explores supporting autonomous process execution within AI-Augmented Business Process Management Systems (ABPMS) using a multi-perspective constraint frame and numeric planning. It aims to enhance framed autonomy in complex process structures.

title: RELIC: Revealed Principles for Learning Interpretable Composable Skills in Multi-Agent Planning
summary: This research introduces RELIC, a framework for learning interpretable composable skills in multi-agent planning scenarios where agents must coordinate despite private internal implementations. It addresses the challenges of developing specialized decision-making skills among independently developed agents.

title: FUSAR-R1: A Large-Scale Reasoning Model for Intelligent Interpretation of SAR Images
summary: This paper introduces FUSAR-R1, a large-scale reasoning model designed for the intelligent interpretation of SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) images. It leverages vision-language model advancements to enhance semantic understanding and human-computer interaction in remote sensing.

title: From Overload to Insights: How AI Agents Can Support Scientists in Analyzing Complex Data
summary: This article explores how AI agents can support scientists in analyzing complex datasets, particularly in environments like European XFEL. It focuses on using agents to streamline data analysis by integrating domain expertise with scattered technical knowledge.

title: AgentBrew: Lifelong Knowledge Brewing from Strong Teachers to Weak LLM Agents
summary: This paper introduces AgentBrew, a method for "lifelong knowledge brewing" that distills a strong teacher's interactive experience into a persistent external memory for weaker LLM agents. This process allows agents to acquire and retain knowledge without weight updates.

title: Beyond Semantic Equivalence: Logical Graphs for LLM Uncertainty Quantification
summary: This research proposes using "Logical Graphs" for uncertainty quantification in Large Language Models, going beyond semantic equivalence to assess reliability for safety-sensitive applications. It addresses the issue of LLMs producing confidently stated yet unreliable outputs.

title: Environment-free Synthetic Data Generation for API-Calling Agents
summary: This paper presents a method for environment-free synthetic data generation to address the bottleneck of training API-calling Large Language Model (LLM) agents. It aims to provide high-quality trajectories without requiring fully implemented API environments.

title: Lomekwi: Resource-Bounded Tool Discovery in LLM Agents
summary: This research introduces Lomekwi, a framework that distinguishes between tool use and resource-bounded tool discovery in LLM agents. It decomposes tool discovery into curiosity and recognition, aiming to improve agents' ability to identify and utilize necessary tools.

title: Training Continuous Chain of Thought Models: A Tale of Two Regimes
summary: This paper explores methods for training Continuous Chain of Thought (CoT) models, which replace verbose reasoning traces with dense latent representations. It investigates different regimes for supervising these latent representations to match verbose reasoning.

title: Expected Free Energy as Belief-Dependent Utility for rho-POMDPs
summary: This research proposes Expected Free Energy as a belief-dependent utility for $\rho$-POMDPs, enabling agents to decide when and what information to gather under partial observability. It directly rewards uncertainty reduction in agent decision-making.

title: Reward-Driven LLM Agent Workflows: Synthesizing POMDP Routing and Self-Correction for Autonomous Decision-Making
summary: This paper introduces an intelligent agent workflow designed to address challenges in LLM agent applications, such as long-horizon planning and dynamic environmental interaction. It focuses on reward-driven mechanisms for autonomous decision-making in agent systems.

title: When LLMs Over-Answer: Measuring and Mitigating Quality Issues in LLM-Based Hardware Description Language Question Answering
summary: This research investigates quality issues like over-answering in LLM-based question answering for Hardware Description Languages. It aims to measure and mitigate imprecise or redundant answers from LLMs in this specific application.

title: Bridging the Information Gap: Semantic Densification and Hindsight Distillation for Cold-Start Prediction
summary: This paper explores methods like semantic densification and hindsight distillation to address the new-user cold-start prediction problem in e-commerce. It focuses on predicting user lifetime value and conversion rate for users with limited interaction history.

title: Otap:Structure-Aware Optimal Transport for Evaluating Planning and Execution in Agent Trajectories
summary: This paper introduces "Otap," a structure-aware optimal transport method for evaluating the planning and execution capabilities of large language model agents. It aims to provide more nuanced evaluation metrics beyond simple success flags for agent trajectories.

title: Fourier Geometric Wind Power Forecasting with Numerical Weather Prediction
summary: This research proposes a Fourier geometric approach combined with numerical weather prediction for accurate short-term wind power forecasting. The method aims to improve grid stability and operational planning by better incorporating atmospheric conditions.

title: Evidence Interfaces Shape How Retrieval-Augmented Readers Use Support
summary: This paper examines how "evidence interfaces," the form in which retrieved evidence is presented, influence a reader's use of support in multi-hop Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems. It highlights potential failures in retrieval windows and how support is utilized.

title: A Diagnostic Framework for AI Agent Behavior
summary: This paper proposes a diagnostic framework for understanding the behavior of AI agents as they operate within complex systems like clinical, political, and social environments. It aims for source-level diagnosis to explain agent behavioral patterns.

title: Is Your Model Thinking or Just Stagnating? PUMA: Diagnosing Reasoning Pathology via Phase-Momentum Alignment
summary: This research introduces "PUMA," a method for diagnosing reasoning pathology in Large Reasoning Models, particularly the "overthinking" paradox in Chain-of-Thought processes. It aims to understand when redundant reasoning occurs without improving accuracy.

title: Toward Anthropomorphic Dialogue: A Closed-Loop Framework for Human-Like Chat Generation, Evaluation, and Preference Alignment
summary: This paper presents "AnthroDial," a closed-loop framework for generating, evaluating, and aligning human-like chat. It aims to create anthropomorphic dialogue systems that maintain persona, relationships, and memory across multi-turn conversations.

title: A Systematic Evaluation of Trajectory Data Curation for LoRA Fine-Tuning of Code Agents
summary: This research systematically evaluates the impact of trajectory data curation on LoRA fine-tuning for building capable code agents. It investigates how the quality and quantity of expert agent trajectories influence model performance.

title: Constrained Path Reasoning: Measuring When Committed Stages Earn Their Cost
summary: This paper introduces Constrained Path Reasoning (CPR), a method for measuring the value and cost-effectiveness of intermediate stages within an LLM reasoning pipeline. It aims to evaluate reasoning efficiency by pairing source-aware path hypotheses with stage-level accounting.

title: LenGuard-GPC: Length Guarding with Guided-Prompt Consistency for Spatial Reasoning Reinforce Learning
summary: This paper presents "LenGuard-GPC," a method for improving spatial reasoning in vision-language models using Reinforcement Learning and guided-prompt consistency. It addresses the verbosity of chain-of-thought reasoning in multi-view spatial tasks.

title: Reinforcement Learning-Guided NSGA-II Enhanced with Gray Relational Coefficient for Multi-Objective Optimization: Application to NASDAQ Portfolio Optimization
summary: This paper applies a Reinforcement Learning-guided NSGA-II algorithm, enhanced with Gray Relational Coefficient, to multi-objective optimization for NASDAQ portfolio management. It aims to optimize portfolios by minimizing risk while maximizing returns.

title: DocOCR-Eval: A Correction-Based Framework for OCR Tool Selection Without Ground Truth
summary: This paper introduces "DocOCR-Eval," a correction-based framework for selecting optimal Optical Character Recognition (OCR) tools without requiring ground truth data. It aims to improve document parsing for downstream tasks like visual question answering.

title: Fully-sensorized smart-eyewear platform for on-device Machine Learning
summary: This paper introduces ARGO, a fully-sensorized smart eyewear platform enabling on-device machine learning with high computational throughput and energy efficiency. It utilizes an integrated Neural Processing Unit (NPU) for local AI processing.

title: LLM Unlearning for Cyber Defense: A Survey on Methods, Challenges, and Emerging Threats
summary: This survey explores methods, challenges, and emerging threats related to LLM unlearning for cyber defense. It addresses the cybersecurity, privacy, and safety risks posed by LLMs' inability to forget sensitive or hazardous information.

title: Operator-Aware Mixed-Precision Tolerance Calibration for Tensor Kernels
summary: This paper introduces a method for operator-aware mixed-precision tolerance calibration for tensor kernels. It aims to improve the correctness testing of AI computations by analyzing error distributions from cloud GPU runs.

title: RouteCost: A Production-Inspired Multi-Stage Framework for Pre-Order Shipping Cost Estimation in E-Commerce
summary: This paper presents "RouteCost," a multi-stage framework for accurate pre-order shipping cost estimation in e-commerce. It addresses the complexities of shipping costs influenced by factors like distance, demand, and dimensional pricing.

title: Orthogonal Gradient Constraints Shape Noisy-Label Memorization Dynamics
summary: This research investigates how orthogonal gradient constraints influence the dynamics of noisy-label memorization in neural networks. It studies a geometric intervention on the optimizer to understand and mitigate memorization-driven overfitting.

title: From Weights to Words: Expressing and Editing Preference Model Inferences in Natural Language
summary: This paper explores a method for expressing and editing inferences from preference models using natural language. It aims to clarify which factors drive decisions inferred by statistical learning algorithms.

title: Token-Level Cross-Modal Transformer with Contrastive Multi-Task Learning for Breast Cancer Subtype Classification and Survival Prediction
summary: Introduces a Transformer-based model with contrastive multi-task learning for improved breast cancer subtype classification and survival prediction by integrating heterogeneous genomic and clinical data.

title: OpenMHC: Accelerating the Science of Wearable Foundation Models
summary: Discusses the potential of wearable foundation models for health monitoring and the challenges researchers face due to the lack of public datasets and open-weight models, proposing OpenMHC to accelerate this science.

title: Quantizing Recursive Reasoning Models
summary: Explores the challenges of quantizing recursive reasoning models, where quantization error accumulates due to the repeated use of weight-tied blocks, affecting model efficiency and accuracy.
