title: Diffusion-corrected Autoregressive Fourier Neural Operator for Droplet Evolution Prediction
summary: Presents a Diffusion-corrected Autoregressive Fourier Neural Operator designed to improve long-horizon prediction of droplet evolution in material jetting, addressing challenges like error accumulation and complex variable coupling.

title: BACON: Budgeted Human Calibration for Modeling and Evaluation with Multiple AI Judges
summary: Proposes BACON, a method for budgeted human calibration of AI judges, to address their potential biases and improve the reliability of AI-based model evaluation for ranking and scoring.

title: Normalized Rewards for Preference Optimization
summary: Introduces normalized rewards to improve direct alignment algorithms (DAAs) like DPO, aiming to prevent over-optimization of implicit reward models and maintain the likelihood of preferred LLM responses.

title: KernelBench-Verified: Do LLM-Generated Kernels Actually Beat PyTorch?
summary: Investigates whether LLM-generated custom CUDA kernels truly outperform PyTorch on benchmarks, revealing instances of "reward hacking" that artificially inflate reported performance.

title: TRACE: Trajectory-Based Safety Patch Learning for LLM Post-Training Realignment
summary: Introduces TRACE, a trajectory-based safety patch learning method designed to quickly re-align large language models for safety after fine-tuning without requiring a full re-alignment process.

title: RobustMAD: Evaluating Real-World Robustness of Multimodal Small Language Models for Deployable Anomaly Detection Assistants
summary: Focuses on evaluating the real-world robustness of multimodal small language models for deployable industrial anomaly detection assistants, addressing challenges like computational demands and privacy for on-site deployment.

title: CIGPO: Contextual Information-Gain Policy Optimization for Multi-Turn Evidence-Reading LLM Agents
summary: Proposes CIGPO (Contextual Information-Gain Policy Optimization) to stabilize the training of multi-turn evidence-reading LLM agents, which otherwise suffer from instability and format-violating responses in reinforcement learning.

title: Learning Structural Manipulability in Gate-Level Netlists Using Graph Neural Networks
summary: Describes a method for learning structural manipulability in gate-level netlists using Graph Neural Networks to characterize node-level flexibility based on topological properties.

title: Let the Data Decide: Supervision Analysis, Capability Trade-offs, and Adaptive Objective Routing in Continued Pre-Training via Off-Policy Distillation
summary: Examines the interactions between training data, objective parameterization, and model capabilities in the continued pre-training of large language models via off-policy distillation, proposing an adaptive objective routing method.

title: Self-Evolving Just-In-Time Memory for Proactive Embodied Safety
summary: Introduces a "Self-Evolving Just-In-Time Memory" system designed to enable embodied agents to proactively identify and mitigate dynamically emerging hazards during closed-loop interactions.

title: High-accuracy Low-Bit KV-Cache Quantization via Local Distribution Restoration
summary: Proposes a high-accuracy low-bit KV-cache quantization method via local distribution restoration to reduce memory and bandwidth overhead in long-context large language models while preserving quality.

title: Benchmarking Machine Learning Models for Multi-Omics-Based Breast Cancer Prediction
summary: Presents a framework for benchmarking machine learning models using multi-omics datasets for breast cancer prediction, focusing on evaluating estrogen receptor status for diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment.

title: Learning Spatio-Temporal Foundation Models from Pure Synthetic Data
summary: Investigates learning Spatio-Temporal Foundation Models (STFMs) exclusively from synthetic data to overcome distributional biases present in real-world pre-training datasets and improve generalizable representations.

title: SOS-LoRA: Static Orthogonal-Subspace Low-Rank Adaptation with Fixed Multi-Scale Scaling
summary: Introduces SOS-LoRA, a new parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that improves upon LoRA by using static orthogonal-subspace adaptation with fixed multi-scale scaling to better handle heterogeneous behaviors in adapted weights.

title: Comprehensive Evaluation of Machine Learning for Type 2 Diabetes Risk Prediction: Large-Scale External Validation and Fairness Analysis
summary: Develops a multi-dimensional framework for comprehensively evaluating machine learning models for Type 2 diabetes risk prediction, focusing on large-scale external validation and fairness analysis to ensure real-world effectiveness.

title: More Than Memory: Task-Conditioned Signed FFN Writes in Long-Context Retrieval
summary: Investigates how a model's Feedforward Network writes influence long-context retrieval performance, testing whether these task-conditioned writes push the retrieval state towards or away from the correct answer.

title: Feature Generation Using LLMs: An Evolutionary Algorithm Approach
summary: Explores an evolutionary algorithm approach for leveraging large language models to automate and enhance feature generation, a critical step in improving machine learning pipeline performance.

title: Discovery by Dreaming: Cross-Domain Recombination in Artificial Memory
summary: This research explores artificial memory, proposing that cross-domain recombination, inspired by how dreams aid memory consolidation, can drive insight and creative discovery in AI systems. It reframes memory as a dynamic process of recombining rather than just storing.

title: From Outcomes to Actions: Leveraging Hindsight for Long-Horizon Language Agent Training
summary: This paper proposes leveraging hindsight in reinforcement learning to improve the training of long-horizon language agents, addressing challenges in distinguishing individual contributions in complex tasks. It aims to enhance LLM-based agents' ability to learn from outcomes over extended interactions.

title: Neural Controlled Differential Equations for EMT-Level Surrogate Modeling of Grid-Forming Inverters
summary: This research applies Neural Controlled Differential Equations for surrogate modeling of grid-forming inverters, addressing challenges in AI-based power electronic converter modeling. It focuses on multi-time-scale hybrid analysis and physics-aware evaluation criteria.

title: Quantifying Ranking Uncertainty in LLM Benchmarks
summary: This paper analyzes methods for quantifying ranking uncertainty in LLM benchmarks, specifically focusing on rank confidence intervals introduced to assess the reliability of model rankings on multi-task leaderboards. It aims to improve the precision of model comparison.

title: AdaSurvMamba: Dynamic Fusion and Semantic Scanning for Multimodal Survival Analysis
summary: This research introduces AdaSurvMamba, a new model utilizing dynamic fusion and semantic scanning for multimodal survival analysis, particularly in cancer prognosis using whole slide images and genomic profiles. It aims to adapt state-space models like Mamba for complex multimodal tasks.

title: Autonomous mechanistic discovery of colorectal cancer vulnerabilities via multi-scale AI swarms
summary: This research utilizes multi-scale AI swarms and multi-agent frameworks to achieve autonomous mechanistic discovery of colorectal cancer vulnerabilities. It aims to bridge the gap between LLM reasoning and biological physics for automated scientific discovery.

title: Preference-based Antibody Expression Ranking: Scaling with Large-scale Weak Supervision
summary: This paper proposes a unified preference-based learning framework for antibody expression ranking, designed to address data scarcity in antibody design. It integrates scarce quantitative expression data with large-scale weak supervision for improved modeling.

title: PsiLogic: Chaos-Aware Active Cancellation for Adam with a Fair Cross-Domain Benchmark
summary: This research introduces PsiLogic, a new chaos-aware optimizer that augments Adam with a dynamic Active Cancellation Term to improve training stability. It adapts its update rule based on training phase, unlike standard adaptive optimizers.

title: A Predict-then-Correct Loop Based on Few-Shot Continuous Contextual Bandit for Demand Forecasting
summary: This study proposes a predict-then-correct loop based on few-shot continuous contextual bandits to improve adaptive retail demand forecasting. The method aims to address challenges when demand shifts quickly and labeled data is sparse in early demand cycles.

title: Retrieval is Enough: Training-Free Interpretability with a Tool-Using Agent
summary: This research proposes a training-free interpretability method for neural network activations, arguing that retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) within a tool-using agent is sufficient for achieving interpretability. It investigates how agents can leverage retrieval for understanding neural networks.

title: EA-RMENet -- Path Loss Prediction in Urban Environments using Deep Learning
summary: This paper proposes EA-RMENet, an Efficient Attention Radio Map Estimation Network, for accurate path loss prediction in urban environments using deep learning. It aims to balance accuracy and computational efficiency in wireless network planning.

title: Compact convolutional neural networks for AI-based drone detection system
summary: This research investigates compact convolutional neural networks for developing AI-based drone detection systems. The aim is to create reliable detection capabilities for first-person-view drones operating in complex electromagnetic environments.

title: Leakage-Robust Evaluation and Data-Scale Sensitivity of Attention-Enhanced Multi-Task Learning for Joint Fault Diagnosis and Remaining Useful Life Estimation
summary: This research investigates leakage-robust evaluation and data-scale sensitivity of attention-enhanced multi-task learning models used for joint fault diagnosis and remaining useful life estimation in predictive maintenance. It addresses challenges in how training and test sets affect reported performance.

title: Building2Building: A Large Scale Benchmark for Generalizable Real-World Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper introduces Building2Building, a new large-scale benchmark designed to evaluate generalizable real-world reinforcement learning. It aims to address the limitations of existing benchmarks by offering greater diversity and complexity for learned policies.

title: Discrete Ricci Curvature on Protein Contact Graphs for Lightweight Fold Classification
summary: This research investigates the use of discrete Ricci curvature on protein contact graphs for lightweight protein fold classification. It aims to provide a structural descriptor for comparing with sequence-based representations and pretrained protein language models.

title: Learning from World Feedback: Why Model Uncertainty Fails as a Risk Signal in Model-Based RL
summary: This research explores why model uncertainty often fails as a risk signal in model-based reinforcement learning, advocating for learning from world feedback instead of internal model proxies. It distills concrete design principles for safe model-based control.

title: Privacy Cost as Equity Input: A Group Fairness Criterion for Differentially Private Machine Learning
summary: This paper proposes privacy cost as an equity input, establishing a new group fairness criterion for differentially private machine learning. It addresses how differential privacy can widen accuracy disparities across demographic groups by treating privacy cost as a fairness concern.

title: Multimodal Attention-based Deep Learning for Emergency Triage with Electronic Health Records
summary: This research applies multimodal attention-based deep learning for improving emergency triage decisions using electronic health records. The system aims to automate and enhance the efficient analysis of patient data, including text complaints and vital signs.

title: CLDRoute: Conditional Latent Diffusion for Routability Map Generation in Physical Design
summary: This paper introduces CLDRoute, a method utilizing Conditional Latent Diffusion for routability map generation in physical design. It aims to improve routability estimation by moving beyond deterministic prediction to reduce post-routing iterations.

title: A Framework for Early Sepsis Prediction via Self-Supervised (JEPA) and Federated Representation Learning
summary: This research proposes a framework for early sepsis prediction using electronic health records, comparing self-supervised Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) and federated representation learning. It addresses challenges like irregular sampling and class imbalance in healthcare data.

title: Building a Neural Network from Scratch: Implementation, Evaluation, and Optimization
summary: This paper presents a self-contained guide to building a neural network from scratch, covering implementation, evaluation, and optimization to bridge the gap between practical usage of libraries and fundamental understanding.

title: Effects of width-dependent model hyperparameters and $\ell_2$-regularization on the loss landscape of two-layer ReLU networks
summary: This research paper investigates the theoretical properties of two-layer ReLU networks, focusing on the effects of width-dependent hyperparameters and L2-regularization on their loss landscape. It aims to improve understanding of deep neural networks, particularly in the presence of weight decay.

title: Half the Experts, All the Code: One-Shot Domain Pruning of Mixture-of-Experts LLMs for Coding
summary: This paper proposes a one-shot domain pruning method for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs specialized in coding, aiming to reduce their size and allow them to run on consumer hardware. The technique helps make powerful open-weight coding models more accessible.

title: Multi-level context Modeling for consistent expert selection in Mixture-of-Experts
summary: This research introduces a multi-level context modeling approach to enhance expert selection in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Transformer models. The method aims to produce more stable and semantically consistent routing decisions compared to current shallow token representation methods.

title: RIMS: Preference Optimization via Smoothed Multi-pair Aggregation for Small-Scale LLM Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: This paper introduces RIMS, a preference optimization technique using smoothed multi-pair aggregation for small-scale language models (SLMs) in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). RIMS aims to make SLMs more robust to noisy retrieved evidence in resource-constrained environments.

title: Committed Before Reasoning: Behavioral Reproduction and Preliminary Activation-Level Evidence of Answer Pre-Commitment in an Open-Weight LLM
summary: This research investigates the phenomenon of "answer pre-commitment" in an open-weight LLM, where the model commits to an answer before generating reasoning, sometimes leading to contradictions. It provides behavioral reproduction and preliminary activation-level evidence of this behavior.

title: Encoding EEG Signals to Examine Human-Like Next-Word Prediction Behaviour in Language Models
summary: This research encodes EEG signals to examine how human-like next-word prediction behavior in language models aligns with human brain responses during reading comprehension. The study aims to compare AI model predictability with neuroscience findings.

title: NOWJ@COLIEE 2026: Adaptive Pipelines for Legal Retrieval and Reasoning
summary: This paper presents the methodologies and results of the NOWJ team's participation in the COLIEE 2026 competition, focusing on adaptive pipelines for legal retrieval and reasoning tasks. It details a four-stage pipeline for legal case retrieval using embedding models.

title: From Memory to Skills: Evidence-Grounded Co-Evolution Governance for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
summary: This paper introduces MSCE, a training-free Memory-Skill Co-Evolution framework designed for long-horizon LLM agents, which transforms retrieved memory traces into executable capabilities. It aims to improve how agents organize and utilize their experience, moving beyond passive context retrieval.

title: OpenLanguageModel: Readable and Composable Small-Language-Model Pretraining for Education and Research
summary: OpenLanguageModel (OLM) is an open-source PyTorch library designed for building and pretraining small language models with transparent, composable architecture for educational and research purposes. It facilitates understanding and experimentation with LLM mechanics.

title: SpecLA: Efficient Speculative Decoding for Linear-Attention Models
summary: This paper presents SpecLA, a method for efficient speculative decoding specifically designed for linear-attention models, aiming to reduce the cost of autoregressive decoding. It proposes a way to verify multiple draft tokens in a single target pass.

title: Are Arithmetic Heuristic Neurons Form-Invariant? A Mechanistic Analysis of Symbols, Text, and Code in LLMs
summary: This research conducts a mechanistic analysis of large language models, investigating whether arithmetic heuristic neurons are form-invariant across different formulations of problems involving symbols, text, and code. It aims to understand the internal circuits and interpretability of LLMs.

title: Though Language Models Err While They Strive: Conformal Prediction for Self-Correcting Scientific Generation
summary: This paper introduces Scientific Feasibility Control (SFC), a graph-structured conformal prediction framework, to improve the reliability of large language models in scientific generation. SFC provides statistical guarantees to prevent LLMs from violating fundamental scientific principles.

title: JOR-Bench: Japanese Operations Research Benchmarks for Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces JOR-Bench, a collection of five Japanese-language benchmarks designed to evaluate the ability of large language models to formulate and solve operations research problems. It provides translated versions of existing English benchmarks for the Japanese context.

title: Cascading versus Joint Modeling for Hierarchical Offensive Language Detection
summary: This research compares cascading versus joint modeling paradigms for fine-grained hierarchical offensive language detection, evaluating their accuracy and parameter count. It aims to provide a controlled comparison of these two modeling approaches.

title: Diagnosing Correctness Probes under Self-Judgement Confounding
summary: This research investigates the confounding effect of self-judgement on correctness probes in language models, where objective correctness often aligns with the model's self-assessment. It constructs conflict cases to diagnose the ambiguity in decoded signals.

title: Schema-Constrained Document-Level Event Argument Extraction with Lightweight LLM Fine-Tuning
summary: This paper proposes a method for schema-constrained document-level event argument extraction using lightweight LLM fine-tuning, which converts documents into structured event records. It addresses challenges like long-range dependencies and cross-sentence context.

title: Group Entropy-Controlled Policy Optimization
summary: This paper introduces Group Entropy-Controlled Policy Optimization, an effective tool in reinforcement learning for large language models. It helps balance the exploration-exploitation trade-off during the LLM alignment process, especially across heterogeneous tasks.

title: Trace-Based On-Policy Distillation for Masked Diffusion Language Models
summary: This paper proposes Trace-Based On-Policy Distillation to address challenges in reasoning-oriented post-training for masked diffusion language models (dLLMs). It offers a method to improve dLLMs, which are an alternative to autoregressive generation.

title: Real-World Evaluation of an AI Agent Drafting Translational Impact Summaries
summary: This study presents a real-world evaluation of an AI agent designed to draft translational impact summaries for research scholars, demonstrating its potential to automate a time-consuming administrative task. The agent serves as a tool to gather and summarize research impact.

title: Learning from Synthetic Data without Model Collapse in Iterative Instruction Tuning
summary: This research investigates 'model collapse' in iterative instruction tuning of large language models (LLMs) when learning from synthetic data and proposes a method to mitigate performance degradation.

title: BLAD: A Historically Contextualized, Multilingual Dataset of Bangladeshi Legal Acts (1799 to 2025)
summary: This paper presents the Bangladesh Legal Acts Dataset (BLAD), a curated, multilingual collection of 1,484 legislative acts from 1799 to 2025, intended as a resource for legal AI research.

title: Scope3Trace: Evidence-Based Identification and Extraction of Scope 3 GHG Emissions from Sustainability Reports
summary: Scope3Trace is introduced as an evidence-based method leveraging large language models (LLMs) to identify and extract Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions from corporate sustainability reports.

title: KyrgyzLLM-Bench: Benchmarking Kyrgyz Language Understanding
summary: KyrgyzLLM-Bench is a new benchmark designed for evaluating large language models (LLMs) specifically for their understanding of the less-resourced Kyrgyz language, addressing limitations of existing multilingual benchmarks.

title: Auditing Question-Order Effects in Large Language Models with the QQ Equality: Mechanism Characterization and a Saturation Caveat
summary: This study develops the QQ equality as an audit criterion to characterize and analyze question-order effects in the sequential judgments made by autoregressive large language models (LLMs).

title: Literary Non-Style in LLM-Generated Text
summary: This research investigates the distinct characteristics of large language model (LLM)-generated text, noting its 'literary non-style' and restricted semantic range compared to human-written content.

title: Robust Summarization of Doctor-Patient Conversations: TalTech Systems for the Beyond Transcription Challenge
summary: TalTech's systems for the Beyond Transcription Challenge focus on robust summarization of doctor-patient conversations, directly generating SOAP notes from long audio recordings without intermediate transcription.

title: AI_LectureNote: A Retrospective Pilot Study of a Post-ASR Workflow for English-Script Rendering and Semantic Drift in Korean-English Medical Lectures
summary: AI_LectureNote describes a retrospective pilot study of a post-ASR workflow for Korean-English medical lectures, designed to improve readability by restoring Latin-script medical terms in study transcripts.

title: EvolvingWorld: An Open-Schema Framework for Co-Evolving Role-Play Agents and World Model in Interactive Literary World
summary: EvolvingWorld is an open-schema framework and benchmark for simulating interactive literary worlds, enabling the co-evolution of role-play agents and the world model itself.

title: Should Missing Modalities Always Be Necessary to Repair for Multi-modal Sentiment Analysis?
summary: This paper re-examines the common 'repair-first' paradigm in multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) under missing modalities, questioning whether repairing every missing modality is always necessary or optimal.

title: Debate-on-Graph: Reliable and Adaptive Reasoning of Large Language Model on Uncertain Knowledge Graph
summary: Debate-on-Graph is proposed as a method to enhance the reliable and adaptive reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) when interacting with uncertain knowledge graphs (KGs) to mitigate hallucinations.

title: Safety That Does Not Transfer: Cross-Lingual Clinical Correctness Drift in Deployable Medical Language Models
summary: This research highlights that safety evaluations of large language models (LLMs) in English and on frontier systems do not transfer to cross-lingual, low-resource clinical settings, leading to 'clinical correctness drift'.

title: Team DACTYL at PAN 2026: Bayesian Data Mixing and Empirical X-risk Minimization for AI-text Detection
summary: Team DACTYL proposes Bayesian Data Mixing and Empirical X-risk Minimization as methods to improve AI-generated text detection classifiers, specifically addressing their performance on out-of-distribution texts.

title: The Librarian Who Refused to Code: Model-Dependent Identity Enactment in LLM Code Generation
summary: This study evaluates the effects of using biographical personas in system prompts on large language model (LLM) code generation, investigating 'model-dependent identity enactment'.

title: How Reliable Are Multimodal Signals of Conversational State? Evidence from Remote Dyadic Collaborative Tasks
summary: This work presents a three-dimensional evaluation framework to assess the reliability of multimodal signals of conversational state, such as cognitive load and conversational power, across different task contexts.

title: Multilingual Sentence Embeddings for Linguistic-Integrated Reliability Audit
summary: This study evaluates the efficacy of multilingual sentence embeddings in replacing translated English input for Linguistic-Integrated Reliability Auditing (LiRA) in multilingual assessment systems.

title: Oracle Gap and Signal Fidelity: A Fixed-Pool Diagnostic for Test-Time Collaboration
summary: This paper introduces 'Oracle Gap' and 'Signal Fidelity' as diagnostic tools to understand when test-time collaboration techniques, like self-consistency, can effectively improve large language model (LLM) reasoning.

title: Tokenizing Crosslingual Homographs
summary: This research explores the challenges of tokenizing crosslingual homographs in multilingual language models, where shared subword vocabularies can lead to uniform treatment of words with different meanings across languages.

title: C$^2$KV: Compressed and Composable KV Cache Reuse for Efficient LLM Inference
summary: C$^2$KV (Compressed and Composable KV Cache Reuse) is a proposed method to improve the efficiency of large language model (LLM) inference by optimizing the key-value (KV) cache for long-context scenarios.

title: Large Language Models for Citation Function Classification
summary: This study evaluates the performance of state-of-the-art large language models (LLMs) for citation function classification, aiming to advance bibliometric analysis and understanding of scientific publication relationships.

title: When to Use Extra Context: Evidence-Grounded Terminology Adaptation for Simultaneous Speech Translation
summary: The paper investigates how to effectively integrate external context into simultaneous speech translation to improve terminology recovery, noting that full document injection is often too broad.

title: ESCUCHA: A Spanish Speech Benchmark for Heterogeneous Acoustic Conditions
summary: This paper introduces ESCUCHA, the first Spanish speech understanding benchmark designed to evaluate large audio language models under realistic and varied acoustic conditions.

title: When a Name Is Not a Name: A Benchmark Dataset and Distilled Reasoning for Culturally Entangled Bangla Homographs in Low-Resource LLMs
summary: This paper introduces a benchmark dataset to evaluate how low-resource LLMs handle culturally entangled Bangla homographs, highlighting the need for cultural knowledge in language models.

title: Zero Hallucination, by Construction: Hallucination-Aware Layered Oversight for Trustworthy Enterprise AI
summary: This paper proposes a 'hallucination-aware layered oversight' framework to address the problem of AI hallucination, aiming to build more trustworthy enterprise AI agents.

title: DeLIVeR: Decomposed Learning for Information-grounded Veracity Recognition via Reinforced Knowledge Graph Exploration
summary: This paper introduces DeLIVeR, a framework that enhances automated fact-checking for LLMs by treating evidence retrieval as reinforced strategic exploration within knowledge graphs to overcome 'query brittleness.'

title: What Transfers Under Source Shift? Definitions, Examples, and Fine-Tuning for Climate Disclosure Classification
summary: This research investigates the transferability of AI models across different sources for climate disclosure classification, exploring definitions, examples, and fine-tuning strategies.

title: An Early Warning of Emerging Biosecurity Risks in Frontier LLMs
summary: This paper warns of emerging biosecurity risks from frontier LLMs, introducing Intern-BioBreaker, a specialized bio-red-teaming model, to assess and understand these potential dangers.

title: Pancasila-Dilemmas: Evaluating Large Language Models on Indonesian Human Value Dilemmas Grounded in Pancasila
summary: This paper introduces 'Pancasila-Dilemmas,' a benchmark for evaluating the value alignment of large language models with Indonesian human values, specifically those grounded in Pancasila.

title: Modeling turn-taking with distant viewing: investigating silence thresholds in human and AI-generated discourse
summary: This study analyzes silence thresholds in human and AI-generated discourse, comparing turn-taking patterns across US sitcoms and synthetic podcasts created with Google NotebookLM.

title: VDAR-Router: Adaptive LLMs Routing via Verbalized Query Difficulty Analysis Retrieval
summary: This paper introduces VDAR-Router, an adaptive system for routing input queries to appropriate large language models based on verbalized query difficulty analysis to optimize cost and performance.

title: How Does Alignment Tuning Shape Representations of Sycophancy and Related Cue-Induced Biases in LLMs?
summary: This paper explores how alignment tuning affects the representation of sycophancy and other cue-induced biases within large language models.

title: VEHBench: A Stage-Local Diagnostic Benchmark for LLM-Assisted Vibration Energy Harvester Design
summary: This paper presents VEHBench, a stage-local diagnostic benchmark for evaluating large language model assistance in the design of vibration energy harvesters for battery-free IoT devices.

title: PPL-Factory: Task-Aware and Budget-Aware Data Selection from Language Modeling to Reasoning
summary: This paper proposes PPL-Factory, a method for task-aware and budget-aware data selection to optimize the fine-tuning of large language models, reducing computational cost while maintaining performance.

title: SWE-Pruner Pro: The Coder LLM Already Knows What to Prune
summary: This paper introduces SWE-Pruner Pro, an improved method for pruning long contexts for coding agents by leveraging the agent's internal representations to identify relevant information for efficient context management.

title: It's Not What You Say, It's How You Say It: Evaluating LLM Responses to Expressions of Belief
summary: This paper evaluates how large language models respond to users' expressions of belief, analyzing whether they accept contextual information or adhere to their prior knowledge, considering the linguistic diversity of such expressions.

title: Automated Discovery Has No Universally Superior Harness
summary: This paper argues that no single universal harness is superior for autonomous discovery systems, emphasizing that these systems are composites of various design choices related to archives, parent selection, exploration, and budget allocation.

title: What Makes Linguistic Representations Good Models of High-Level Visual Perception in the Human Brain?
summary: This research investigates the factors that make linguistic representations from language models effective predictors of human brain responses to naturalistic images in high-level visual regions.

title: ForensicNet: Lightweight Attention-Enhanced MobileNetV2 for Automated Face Identification
summary: This paper introduces ForensicNet, a lightweight, attention-enhanced deep learning framework based on MobileNetV2, designed for automated face identification in challenging forensic environments.

title: 3D FaceShell: Attribute Transfer in 3D Face Avatars as a VLM Defense Mechanism
summary: This paper introduces 3D FaceShell, a method for attribute transfer in 3D face avatars that acts as a defense mechanism against vision-language models inferring sensitive attributes from rendered images.

title: Moving Like a Human: Ego-Motion-Normalized Temporal Signatures for Real-Time Aerial Person Tracking on Milliwatt-Class Hardware
summary: This paper proposes a system using ego-motion-normalized temporal signatures for real-time aerial person tracking on drones, optimized for milliwatt-class hardware.

title: GenSyn10: A Multi-Generative AI Dataset For Benchmarking Image Classification
summary: Introduces GenSyn10, a synthetic image dataset aligned with CIFAR-10, designed for benchmarking image classification models to detect generative AI outputs. It aims to evaluate the reliability of detectors against unseen generators.

title: MAC 2026: Advancing Micro-Action Analysis Towards Fine-Grained Understanding
summary: Presents MAC 2026, a research effort focused on advancing micro-action analysis to achieve fine-grained understanding of subtle human behaviors. It addresses the challenges in annotating, modeling, and evaluating these short-duration patterns.

title: A Synthetic 3D Gear Dataset for Manufacturing Quality Inspection (MFGNet-Gear)
summary: Introduces MFGNet-Gear, a synthetic 3D gear dataset developed for manufacturing quality inspection using data-driven deep learning methods. It aims to automate the assessment of dimensional accuracy, surface quality, and shape in manufactured parts.

title: Strength-Parity Ensembling with Parameter-Isolated Experts for Multi-Task Affect Recognition
summary: Proposes strength-parity ensembling with parameter-isolated experts to improve multi-task affect recognition, focusing on joint valence-arousal estimation, expression recognition, and action-unit detection. It investigates how to effectively combine ensemble members.

title: Beyond Target Scores: Measuring Off-Target Drift in Diffusion-Based Medical Image Editing
summary: Discusses the challenge of measuring off-target drift in diffusion-based medical image editing, proposing an evaluation method beyond simple target scores. It addresses how models can appear successful while potentially introducing unintended changes in clinical imaging.

title: It Depends on the Dataset: When a Brain-Encoding Model's Predicted Responses Beat Their Visual Backbone for Video Memorability
summary: Explores how brain-encoding foundation models, which predict fMRI responses to multimedia, can be used as a feature lens for forecasting video memorability. It investigates the utility of these predicted responses for a downstream human-behavior task.

title: SLT: Robust Quantum Neural Networks for Noisy-Label Medical Image Classification via Supermartingale-based Label Transition
summary: Proposes SLT, a method using robust Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) with Supermartingale-based Label Transition for noisy-label medical image classification. It aims to address the challenges of noisy labels in small-scale medical datasets.

title: A${}^2$BM: Alignment-Aware Bridge Matching for Image-to-Image Translation
summary: Introduces A²BM (Alignment-Aware Bridge Matching), a novel framework for paired image-to-image translation that extends diffusion models. It aims to improve various computer vision tasks like image editing and domain adaptation.

title: Emergent Hierarchical Monosemantic Neurons from the Group-Contrastive Forward-Forward Algorithm
summary: Investigates emergent hierarchical monosemantic neurons using the Group-Contrastive Forward-Forward Algorithm to advance mechanistic interpretability in neural networks. It addresses limitations found in sparse dictionary learning methods for understanding representations.

title: Rethinking Feature Reliance Evaluation with Semantically Matched Suppression
summary: Proposes a new method called Semantically Matched Suppression to re-evaluate how visual recognition models rely on features like shape, texture, or color. It aims to provide a more accurate interpretation of model behavior beyond cue-conflict studies.

title: FedDP-PALD: A Privacy-Preserving Federated Latent Diffusion Framework with Prototype Aggregation for Medical Data Synthesis
summary: Introduces FedDP-PALD, a privacy-preserving federated latent diffusion framework with prototype aggregation for synthesizing medical data. It enables development of diagnostic models across institutions while adhering to strict privacy regulations.

title: Med-OPD: Improving Medical Vision-Language Models via Evidence-Aware On-Policy Distillation
summary: Proposes Med-OPD, a method utilizing evidence-aware on-policy distillation to improve Medical Vision-Language Models (Med-VLMs). It aims to enhance reliable reasoning from fine-grained visual evidence, preventing models from relying solely on language priors.

title: Dual-Domain Self-Supervised Artifact Removal Framework for Photoacoustic Computed Tomography
summary: Presenting a dual-domain self-supervised framework for artifact removal in Photoacoustic Computed Tomography (PACT). It addresses challenges from reconstruction artifacts by exploiting distinct artifact patterns between different reconstruction algorithms.

title: LookME: Lookup-Based Multimodal Embeddings for Layer Injection in Vision-Language Models
summary: Introduces LookME (Lookup-Based Multimodal Embeddings) for layer injection in Vision-Language Models (VLMs). This method aims to improve VLM performance while addressing deployment limitations in resource-constrained environments by optimizing memory usage.

title: CoBind: Stage-Aware Compositional Binding for Training-Free Text-to-Image Generation
summary: Introduces CoBind, a stage-aware compositional binding method for training-free text-to-image generation in diffusion models. It aims to address failures in handling complex prompts by improving object composition and attribute assignment.

title: SaaF: Scene-Specific Ambiguity-Aware 3D Language Fields towards Interactive Real-World Object Retrieval
summary: Proposes SaaF (Scene-specific Ambiguity-aware 3D Language Fields), a novel Gaussian Splatting-based 3D language field for interactive real-world object retrieval. This capability is crucial for service robots operating in complex environments.

title: Seeing What Is Actually There: PriVE-Bench and PriVE-Tools for Counterfactual Evaluation of Agentic Visual Evidence in VLMs
summary: Introduces PriVE-Bench and PriVE-Tools for counterfactual evaluation of agentic visual evidence in Vision-Language Models (VLMs). These tools aim to diagnose when VLMs rely on language priors rather than grounding predictions in the actual image.

title: xperception -- Making Robotic Grasping Easier
summary: Introduces xperception, a solution aimed at making robotic grasping easier and more flexible for high-mix low-volume manufacturing. It addresses the limitations of conventional vision systems that require extensive data collection and retraining.

title: Depth-Regularized JEPA World Models Learn More Transferable Representations from Real Outdoor Robot Data
summary: Proposes depth-regularized JEPA world models to learn more transferable representations from real outdoor robot data. This approach aims to improve the robust dynamics learning of world models in visually complex and unpredictable robot environments.

title: Eddy-VL 1.9B: Structural Pruning and Layered Distillation for Edge-Deployable Multimodal Embedding
summary: Introduces Eddy-VL 1.9B, a compressed multimodal embedding model built through structural pruning and layered distillation for edge-deployable vision-language retrieval. It is designed for offline, low-latency applications in environments without cloud APIs.

title: Deep Learning-based Filtering for Video Coding: A Survey on Architectures, Algorithms, and Complexity Analysis
summary: As Ultra-High-Definition (UHD) displays and immersive media services become ubiquitous in the Internet of Things (IoT) and Consumer Electronics (CE) sectors, including 8K display and mobile devices, the demand for high-efficiency video coding is unprecedented. While Deep Learning-based Filtering (DLF) has emerged as a promising solution to mitigate compression artifacts inherent in standards like High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC/H.265) and Versatile Video Coding (VVC/H.266), its deployment in CE devices is severely constrained by computational complexity, memory bandwidth, and power consumption. To bridge the gap between academic research and practical deployment, this paper presents a comprehensive, hardware-oriented survey of DLF techniques. We propose a systematic three-dimensional taxonomy classifying methods into (1) Integration Scheme within the Video Coding, (2) Coding Information Utilization, and (3) Network Design Strategy. Unlike prior reviews, this work critically analyzes the trade-offs between Rate-Distortion (RD) performance and hardware feasibility, highlighting the evolution from heavy, performance-oriented models to lightweight, hardware-friendly architectures targeting Neural Processing Units (NPUs). Furthermore, we incorporate the latest standardization activities from the Joint Video Experts Team (JVET) on Neural Network-based Video Coding (NNVC) to provide realistic guidelines. We also identify open challenges such as real-time inference latency and error propagation, providing a roadmap toward robust, low-power intelligent video coding in next-generation CE vision endpoints.

title: The Devil is in the Dark Pixels: Toward Brightness Bias-Robust Denoising
summary: In this paper, we reveal an important yet overlooked problem in image denoising: under signal-dependent camera noise models, dark regions suffer from inherently low Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR), as signal intensity decays far faster than noise variance diminishes, making detail recovery in dark areas fundamentally challenging. Yet rather than compensating for this difficulty, MSE-trained denoisers exacerbate it -- reconstructing dark pixels up to 6x worse relative to their per-band noise floor. This bias stems from two compounding factors: signal-dependent noise inflates bright-pixel residuals, and the network's Jacobian norm increases monotonically with brightness. Together, these cause bright regions to chronically dominate gradient updates at the expense of dark ones. To this end, we propose Brightness Bias-Robust Denoising (BBRD), a drop-in replacement for MSE loss that partitions pixels into brightness bands, normalizes per-band error by empirical noise variance, and applies Group Distributionally Robust Optimization (Group-DRO) to dynamically upweight whichever band is currently worst, with zero additional parameters or inference cost. Across 8 architectures and 2 datasets in our experiments, BBRD is the only method among 13 tested alternatives that improves each brightness band simultaneously, achieving up to +0.45 dB on dark bands, +0.32 dB on bright bands, and +0.65 dB aggregate Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) on SIDD, with the largest per-band gains in the darkest regions where detail recovery matters most. Code is available at https://github.com/xmed-lab/BBRD

title: Art Beyond Semantics: Sheaf-Informed Contrastive Learning for Multi-Relational Representations
summary: Understanding a painting is never a single act. Art historians may analyze the same work through concepts of style, iconography, or historical context, dimensions that are not interchangeable, and each carries distinct semantic relationships between the visual and the textual. Vision-Language Models (VLMs) like CLIP, which learn a single shared embedding space, collapse this richness into a single homogeneous alignment, thereby losing the multi-relational structure that defines art-historical reasoning. We introduce CANVAS (Contrastive Art-aware Network for Vision-Language Alignment with Sheaves), a framework for learning relation-aware multimodal representations inspired by sheaf theory. Each artwork is projected into multiple embeddings conditioned on the type of relation (i.e., the context), and a novel contrastive loss encodes contextual information during training, with no dependency on external data at inference. We evaluate on three newly introduced benchmarks of artworks for multi-relational art understanding: WikiArt+, derived from WikiArt and Wikipedia, HertzianaDP, from the Bibliotheca Hertziana collection, and SemArt+, refined from the SemArt dataset. In multimodal retrieval and art understanding, CANVAS outperforms the baselines, supporting the view that multi-relational alignment is not just theoretically motivated but also practically essential.

title: GMoT: Gated Motion-Aware Tokenization for Fine-Grained Micro-Gesture Video Reasoning with Multimodal LLMs
summary: Micro-gesture recognition demands the detection of fleeting, spatially localized movements that are frequently overwhelmed by dominant static appearances and background noise. While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) excel at general video understanding, they inherently struggle with subtle kinematics and often rely on static posture priors. To this end, we propose GMoT, a Gated Motion-Aware Tokenization module that explicitly distills sparse kinematic evidence into a compact sequence prior to temporal modeling. GMoT dynamically spotlights action-relevant regions via spatially weighted pooling, extracts adjacent-frame temporal differencing to capture precise motion energy, and adaptively fuses these cues into the visual stream using a conservatively initialized semantic gate. To transition from simple classification to evidence-grounded reasoning, we further introduce a progressive reward-guided policy refinement paradigm, supported by a semi-supervised annotation pipeline that generates anatomically focused captions. Beyond achieving the best Top-1 accuracy among the compared methods on iMiGUE (67.32\%) and SMG (73.11\%), improving the Qwen3-VL-8B baseline by +6.80 and +3.11 points, our framework introduces Body-Region Grounding (BRG) Recall as an anatomical-grounding proxy conditioned on correct predictions, together with an overlapping-label cross-domain transfer protocol between iMiGUE and SMG. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that our GMoT-augmented model improves in-domain accuracy, retains clear gains under label-preserving corruptions, and improves accuracy-oriented cross-domain transfer under explicit small-split caveats while maintaining high anatomical grounding in its generated rationales.

title: SGMCE: Segment-Grounded Morphological Concept Explanation for Malaria Parasite Species Identification in Thick Blood Smears
summary: Malaria diagnosis in endemic regions depends on species-level identification of Plasmodium parasites in thick blood smears, but deep learning detectors classify detections without providing morphological evidence for their predictions, limiting the ability of microscopists to audit those predictions at the case level. We present SGMCE (Segment-Grounded Morphological Concept Explanation), a post-hoc explanation framework that requires no additional training, no morphological annotations, and no labelled explanation data, yet produces per-detection natural-language explanations anchored in thick-smear morphology. For each detection, SGMCE extracts mask-guided crop thumbnails, computes fourteen handcrafted computer-vision morphological features (shape, colour, chromatin, haemozoin pigment) using adaptive within-mask thresholds, and queries GPT-4o with both visual evidence and computed measurements, conditioned on a thick-smear-specific knowledge base compiled from the World Health Organization bench aids. The primary output is a structured explanation identifying which morphological features support the detected species and why the competing species are excluded. Explanations are validated by four automatic metrics: Knowledge-Base Consistency (KBC), CV-Claim Faithfulness (CCF), Discriminativeness Score (DS), and LLM-as-Judge (LLMj). A sentence-level semantic scoring rule with species-aware negation filtering resolves the vocabulary mismatch between clinical prose and knowledge-base terms. Across 737 detections from 139 thick-smear images spanning four Plasmodium species and white blood cells, parasite-class mean KBC is 0.91, mean DS is 0.99, and mean CCF is 0.97, while a per-rule CCF breakdown confirms that the CV-grounded claims made by the vision-language model are consistent with the measurements they cite.

title: RegionFM: Interpretable Region-Based Brain MRI Classification Using Foundation Model Embeddings
summary: Foundation models provide powerful representations for brain MRI analysis, but their predictions remain difficult to interpret in anatomically meaningful terms. Clinical assessment of brain MRI is commonly organized around anatomically defined structures and regional abnormalities, whereas conventional explanation methods typically produce voxel- or patch-level importance maps that do not explicitly quantify the contributions of individual brain regions. To address this mismatch, we propose RegionFM, an interpretable framework that integrates anatomical segmentation with brain MRI foundation-model embeddings. RegionFM first divides each MRI scan into anatomical regions and constructs a separate MRI volume for each region. A frozen foundation model then encodes each region into an embedding, and a region-additive logistic model combines these embeddings such that every anatomical region contributes an explicit scalar term to the final prediction. This formulation supports both subject-level and cohort-level analyses of regional contributions. We evaluate RegionFM on cognitive-impairment classification using embeddings from multiple pretrained brain MRI foundation models. The results show that RegionFM maintains performance comparable to less interpretable fine-tuning approaches while providing anatomically grounded explanations. Randomized embedding ablations yield near-chance performance, indicating that the predictions rely on meaningful structure captured by the foundation-model embeddings rather than simple feature statistics. Overall, RegionFM better aligns model explanations with anatomy-based clinical reasoning while maintaining competitive predictive performance.

title: CRISP: Pre-LLM Yet Text-Driven Visual Token Pruning for Efficient LVLM Inference
summary: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) typically require processing hundreds to thousands of visual tokens, leading to substantial inference overhead. Existing visual token pruning methods either operate before the LLM using text-agnostic heuristics or prune inside the LLM at the cost of efficiency and noisy cross-modal attention. To address these limitations, we propose CRISP, a pre-LLM yet text-driven visual token pruning framework that preserves both instruction-relevant evidence and essential scene context. CRISP works in a two-stage pipeline: Stage 1 first identifies text-aligned visual tokens, and Stage 2 enhances contextual completeness through semantic diversity. Extensive experiments on LLaVA-1.5 and LLaVA-NeXT demonstrate that CRISP achieves superior performance retention under aggressive pruning ratios, maintaining up to 99.5% accuracy while reducing inference cost and latency by more than 2 times. CRISP serves as a practical solution for efficient LVLM inference, especially in resource-constrained scenarios.

title: Localization-Infused Vision-Language Semantic Fusion for Text-Guided Medical Image Segmentation
summary: Medical image segmentation is essential for modern computer-aided medicine. Recently, text-guided segmentation has shown promise by incorporating clinician-formulated textual reports as semantic guidance for image segmentation. These reports describe target appearance, location, and neighboring anatomy, providing explicit guidance for localization and delineation. Existing text-guided segmentation methods typically extract textual semantics implicitly through a pretrained text encoder and then integrate vision-language semantics via straightforward image-text feature fusion. However, these methods do not explicitly capture target-oriented information embedded in textual reports, particularly target location, and do not explore multi-level information fusion strategies beyond basic feature-level fusion, limiting the extraction and integration of critical textual semantics. In this study, we propose LoG, a localization-infused vision-language fusion framework for text-guided medical image segmentation. By jointly performing multi-scale target localization tasks, LoG explicitly captures target-oriented vision-language semantics and enables three-level localization-infused semantic fusion: (i) localization-guided feature fusion that directly infuses location-relevant semantics into visual features, (ii) localization-gated attention fusion that redirects multi-scale localization predictions to reinforce critical regions, and (iii) localization-constrained loss fusion that supervises segmentation based on spatial consistency with target localization. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets, involving three medical imaging modalities with paired textual reports, demonstrate that LoG achieves Dice scores of 91.59%, 80.71%, and 94.59% on QaTa-COV19, MosMedData+, and Kvasir-SEG, respectively, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art medical image segmentation methods.

title: Local Brushstroke Quality Assessment via Vision-Language Feedback
summary: This paper investigates whether multimodal LLMs can evaluate local brushstroke quality in calligraphy and generate educationally useful natural language feedback. We construct an evaluation framework in which three multimodal LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet 4, and Gemini 2.5 Flash) assess before-after image pairs of calligraphic works using a five-point ordinal scale, and compare their outputs against scores assigned by three expert calligraphers. We additionally examine a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) variant of Claude as a preliminary condition. Results show that all models achieve useful levels of absolute score accuracy (MAE), with GPT-4o performing best (MAE = 0.885). However, none of the models produce statistically significant overall rank correlations with human experts (Kendall's tau). Vocabulary analysis of generated rationales reveals characteristic evaluative biases in each model, and RAG is shown to improve rank correlation while worsening absolute accuracy, constituting an important negative result for text-based rule injection.

title: DMFNet: Dual-Backbone Multiscale Fusion Network for Urban Scene Classification
summary: This article presents DMFNet, a dual-backbone multiscale feature fusion framework with residual feature propagation and spatial attention for remote sensing scene classification. Existing approaches often face challenges in effectively capturing multiscale feature interactions and learning robust feature representations from complex aerial scenes with high intra-class variability and inter-class similarity. To address these limitations, the proposed framework employs two pretrained backbone networks to extract diverse hierarchical feature representations. A multiscale feature fusion mechanism with residual feature propagation is introduced to enhance feature interaction across multiple resolution levels. In addition, a spatial attention module is introduced to emphasize informative spatial regions in multi-object scenes. Further, a two-stage training strategy consisting of backbone freezing followed by selective fine-tuning is adopted to ensure stable optimization and improved generalization. Experiments conducted on the benchmark AID dataset demonstrate that the DMFNet achieves an average accuracy of 97.46\% $\pm$ 0.14\%. Ablative analysis further show the importance of various components in unison.

title: Privacy-Aware Synthetic Video Benchmarking and Relational Evaluation for Worker-Under-Suspended-Load Detection
summary: Publicly shareable construction-video benchmarks remain scarce, especially for safety-critical hazards that are rare, dangerous to stage, and difficult to release. We study worker under suspended load, a relational hazard that depends on worker-load geometry and temporal persistence rather than object detection alone. We introduce SynthSite, a focused synthetic video benchmark of 55 clips spanning varied load configurations, viewpoints, clutter, occlusions, and surveillance conditions, together with a privacy-aware hybrid generation workflow that supports both publicly shareable benchmark creation and privacy-constrained synthetic video generation. We then ask whether worker appearance can be suppressed without undermining downstream hazard recognition. Under five whole-body privacy conditions, we evaluate worker and load retention, localization stability, and clip-level hazard recognition. We find that structure-preserving obfuscations retain substantially more downstream utility than appearance-smoothing baselines, and that preserving a raw visual reference alone does not guarantee the strongest agreement with human hazard labels. These findings suggest that privacy evaluation for construction safety analytics should assess not only appearance suppression, but also preservation of the geometric cues required for hazard reasoning. Our dataset and code are available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/govtech/SynthSite .

title: PhysAgent: Reflective Agentic Physics Control for Physically Plausible Video Generation
summary: Recent advances in physics-grounded video generation leverage physics simulation as a physical prior to guide video synthesis toward physically plausible outcomes. The simulation process is controlled by physical specifications, which are typically generated by a vision-language model in a single pass. Such one-shot prediction often fails to accurately translate user intent into executable simulations, particularly for fine-grained object dynamics, complex motion trajectories, and temporally structured interactions. In this paper, we propose PhysAgent, a reflective agentic framework that closes the loop among physical program generation, physics simulation, stage-specific verification, and targeted program repair. Beyond improving the control of coupled physical parameters, our framework enables the agent to progressively realize complex trajectories, multi-stage interactions, and precise event outcomes by treating each physical program as an executable hypothesis. In addition, we design a set of physics-control APIs to support more stable and complex motion behaviors. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PhysAgent produces more physically plausible videos, achieves better prompt alignment, and generalizes more effectively across diverse physical scenarios.

title: Spatial Transport of Integration Error in Generative ODEs
summary: A trained flow or diffusion model is usually run with only a handful of solver steps, and the integration error this leaves behind is unevenly distributed across the image. We ask where that error is injected and how it reaches the endpoint, and answer with a signed source-and-transport accounting of few-step integration error, tested to first order. A perturbation experiment on five models at 256^2 resolution shows the learned dynamics spread local disturbances widely: near the start of sampling, under 10% of the summed endpoint response remains at the source. Signed one-step truncation residuals, propagated through the model's own linearized dynamics, reconstruct much of the endpoint error's direction and regional structure (cosine 0.81-0.87), and a region's error owes more to what arrives from elsewhere than to its own injection. Structure-destroying nulls, with protocols frozen before evaluation, locate what carries the account: randomizing contribution signs halves it, and reassigning which region receives each contribution, with content, norms, and signs intact, destroys it entirely. Where the injections land is readable from the model itself. The variation of its velocity or prediction field along the trajectory, a structure that emerges during training, predicts the final per-region gap (within-image rho of 0.57-0.70 on fine trajectories, weaker from the cheap solve alone). The prediction is partial because endpoint error depends not only on injected magnitude but on its sign, timing, and transport through the learned dynamics. A training penalty on the injected variation lowers few-step error, so the structure is one a model can be trained to change.

title: OmniStyle-INR: Universal and Multimodal Style Transfer for INRs
summary: Style transfer remains a fundamental and highly important task across various data modalities, enabling creative manipulation conditioned by both reference images and textual descriptions. Recently, methods utilizing Gaussian Splatting have emerged as a unified representation for 2D images, video, 3D scenes, and 4D dynamics. However, representing videos and 2D images with Gaussian Splatting is structurally sub-optimal for dense continuous domains. The number of required Gaussians often approaches the total number of pixels, raising questions about the actual utility of such a representation for these specific modalities. In contrast, Implicit Neural Representations have established themselves as a much more popular and natural choice across all these data domains. Implicit Neural Representations naturally provide significant advantages, including data compression, inherent capabilities for super resolution, and seamless integration with deep generative models. To this end, we introduce OmniStyle-INR, a novel framework that leverages network-based continuous representations as a truly universal domain. Our approach successfully performs high-quality style transfer across all visual modalities, guided seamlessly by both text prompts and visual exemplars.

title: Disentangling Model and Human Data Uncertainty in Apparent Facial Age Estimation
summary: Estimating the apparent age of individuals from facial images is challenging due to the subjective nature of perception and the inherent variability of the data. We investigate the role of uncertainty estimation, attributing uncertainty jointly to a lack of knowledge (epistemic) or inherent noise/chance (aleatoric). Leveraging the APPA-REAL dataset, we train Bayesian Neural Networks on datasets of varying sizes using three BNN approximations: MC-DropConnect, Flipout, and Deep Ensembles using supervision on human aleatoric uncertainty available in the APPA-REAL dataset. Each model outputs both the predicted apparent age and the amount of aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty. Our results confirm the hypothesis that the inherent aleatoric uncertainty remains stable across dataset sizes, while epistemic uncertainty increases as training data decreases. These findings demonstrate that different sources of uncertainty can be quantified in face age estimation.

title: Apple-$\pi$: Benchmarking Thinking with Video Towards Law-Grounded Physical Intelligence
summary: Modern video generation models are increasingly hailed as emerging world models with an internalized grasp of physical law. Yet existing benchmarks largely evaluate physical plausibility only at the output level, without verifying whether the model arrives there through a faithful, law-grounded reasoning process. We introduce Apple-PI, the first benchmark that anchors video-model evaluation explicitly in physical laws. Apple-PI comprises three components. 1) Orchard: a dataset of 400 videos covering ten canonical tasks in classical mechanics. It separates single-law tasks for confounder-free diagnosis from multi-law tasks for probing generalization. 2) Benchmark Protocol: a three-stage protocol based on scientific reasoning, including Perception, Formulation, and Deduction. It uses chain-of-frames prompting on infographic-annotated first frames, treating the generated video as the model's visible reasoning trace. 3) Evaluation Suite: a hybrid evaluation suite that combines MLLM-based subjective scoring with physics-law-grounded objective measures. This enables stage-resolved diagnosis of not only whether a model fails, but where it fails. Benchmarking 11 models shows that current video models remain far from reliable law-grounded world simulators, with the best video model scoring only 0.473. Our stage-, pillar-, and source-resolved analyses further expose a Perception-to-Formulation-to-Deduction bottleneck, weak multi-law state transfer, and a persistent Sim-to-Real gap. These findings position Apple-PI as a diagnostic foundation for guiding future video models toward world models with law-grounded physical intelligence.

title: Think, Plan, Paint: Layout-Aware Reasoning for Controllable Image Generation in Unified Models
summary: Unified Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) offer a promising paradigm for unifying visual understanding and generation, yet they still struggle to follow complex spatial instructions and logical constraints in controllable image generation. To address this gap, we present ATLAS, a unified framework that equips MLLMs with a human-like "Think, Plan, and Paint" paradigm. We adopt layout as the shared representation that connects the three stages, enabling the model to reason about spatial requirements, plan explicit object arrangements, and render the final image. We further improve plan-to-image fidelity with reinforcement-learning-based layout alignment. We instantiate ATLAS at 7B and 80B scales, achieving state-of-the-art performance among MLLMs on image generation benchmarks and an average 65.31% improvement over existing layout-based unified MLLMs. On spatially related tasks, ATLAS obtains an average 23.06% gain over the base models. Through the same layout interface, ATLAS also supports instruction-guided editing and multimodal grounding. We further introduce ATLAS-Reasoning, a benchmark for evaluating generation under complex spatial instructions.

title: One Modality to Forget Them All: Enhancing Cross-Modal Unlearning in Vision-Language Models
summary: Machine unlearning is widely used to remove hazardous knowledge from large language models. Modern Vision-Language Models (VLMs), however, process both text and visual inputs, raising a fundamental security question: does unlearning in one modality transfer to the other? We present the first systematic, bidirectional study of cross-modal unlearning transfer across three VLM architectures: LLaVA-1.5 (MLP projection), InstructBLIP (Q-Former), and IDEFICS (gated cross-attention). We find that unlearning transfers across modalities, but the transfer is asymmetric and incomplete. In some cases, text unlearning strongly transfers to vision. However, this robustness is not preserved under typographic attacks that manipulate the visual presentation of text. Under such attacks, previously unlearned knowledge can be readily recovered, indicating shallow unlearning. To address the transfer gap and shallow robustness, we propose \textsc{CrossInf}, an influence-guided mitigation strategy. Motivated by the observation that different model components contribute unequally to cross-modal transfer, \textsc{CrossInf} focuses unlearning on transformer blocks that most influence cross-modal generalization. It reduces the transfer gap by more than half in architectures with strong fusion, while preserving model utility. It also improves robustness under typographic attacks, reducing the attack success rate to near zero. We further conduct human evaluation with three annotators ($\kappa{=}0.77$) to validate our findings. Finally, we analyze shallow unlearning using Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA), providing insights into the observed transfer behavior and robustness limitations.

title: Spectral-Morphological Attention U-Net: An Efficient Network for Active Wildfire Detection
summary: Over the past decades, the frequency of global wildfires has been increasing steadily. Therefore, if the fire can be detected and precisely located at an early stage, the potential hazards caused by it can be minimized to the greatest extent. The machine learning methods based on satellite images, due to their ability to automatically monitor extremely remote and vast areas, have shown great potential for application in the field of wildfire detection. To address this challenge, we proposed a new model named spectral-morphological attention U-Net(SMA-UNet), which includes a spectral attention module, a residual attention UNet backbone, a channel-spatial modulator, and a pair of differentiable morphological gates. We trained and evaluated this model with two datasets. These modules, excluding the backbone, are used to detect active fire events for the first time, especially the pair of differentiable morphological gates, which is innovatively developed. The proposed model achieved the highest scores in both datasets (e.g., intersection over union 75.16% in TS-SatFire, 22.50% in Sen2Fire). By conducting ablation studies of each module, we compared their independent contributions and tested their combinations. Ultimately, the integration of these modules yields a highly robust framework that significantly improves segmentation consistency across diverse and complex environmental conditions. Future work will focus on validating the proposed architecture across large-scale, multi-regional datasets from different satellite sensors to establish its broader generalizability for global wildfire detection.

title: WeedExpert-R1: Incentivizing Botanical Reasoning in MLLMs with Reinforcement Learning for Precision Weed Grounding
summary: Precision weed control requires species-level identification and instance-level localization. However, conventional object detectors use a closed vocabulary, limiting their deployment across regions, and cannot explain their predictions in complex agricultural scenes. Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) offer visual grounding and reasoning capabilities, but insufficient botanical knowledge can cause hallucinations in fine-grained weed identification. This study introduces WeedExpert-R1, a multimodal model that learns visually grounded botanical reasoning through verifiable rewards. A domain-specific Chain-of-Thought synthesis pipeline combines a human-curated botanical trait dictionary with an Auditor-Synthesizer LLM workflow to generate reasoning data for supervised fine-tuning. Group Relative Policy Optimization is then applied with rewards for format, accuracy, instance count, and response length. Across 37 weed species from six datasets, WeedExpert-R1-4B achieved 75.82 percent exact-set precision at an IoU threshold of 0.5, 89.30 percent precision, and 87.81 percent recall. It outperformed proprietary models, including GPT-5.4 and Gemini-3.1-Pro, and larger open-source models, including Qwen3-VL-30B-Instruct and Gemma-4-31B-it. Results on unseen species further demonstrate its open-vocabulary capability and potential for deployment across diverse regions and crops without retraining.
